unique_issues.title: BUG: find_filename misses filenames when fenced block markers are indented
unique_issues.body:
## Summary

`find_filename` can miss a valid filename when the surrounding fenced block markers have leading whitespace.

Aider already supports recovering filenames from fenced blocks, and the `find_filename` docstring includes an indented fence example. In the current implementation, the loop stops early because it checks the raw line with `line.startswith("```")` instead of checking the stripped line.

## Steps to reproduce

Check out Aider main at commit `5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c`.

Add the following test inside `TestUtils` in `tests/basic/test_editblock.py`:

```python
def test_find_filename_with_indented_fences(self):
    fence = ("```", "```")
    valid_fnames = ["dir/file3.py"]

    lines = ["  ```python", "file3.py", "  ```"]

    self.assertEqual(
        eb.find_filename(lines, fence, valid_fnames),
        "dir/file3.py",
    )
```

Run:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/basic/test_editblock.py -q
```

## Expected behavior

`find_filename` should treat indented fenced markers the same way as non-indented fenced markers when looking back for a filename, and return:

```text
dir/file3.py
```

## Actual behavior

The added regression test fails because `find_filename` returns `None`:

```text
FAILED tests/basic/test_editblock.py::TestUtils::test_find_filename_with_indented_fences
AssertionError: None != 'dir/file3.py'

1 failed, 25 passed in 1.32s
```

## Impact

When an LLM returns a SEARCH/REPLACE block with slightly indented fenced markers, Aider may fail to recover the filename even though the filename is present and matches a known repo file. This can make an otherwise valid edit block fail with a missing filename error.

## Root cause

Inside `find_filename`, each candidate line is first normalized by `strip_filename(line, fence)`, which strips whitespace before checking for fences.

But the continuation check uses the raw line:

```python
if not line.startswith(fence[0]) and not line.startswith(triple_backticks):
    break
```

For an indented fence like `"  ```"`, this condition becomes true and the loop breaks before it reaches the filename line.

## Possible fix direction

Use a stripped line for the fence-continuation check:

```python
stripped = line.strip()
if not stripped.startswith(fence[0]) and not stripped.startswith(triple_backticks):
    break
```

A regression test should cover both plain fenced blocks and indented fenced blocks.

## Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.3.dev`, `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c`  
Python: focused unit-level reproduction  
Operating system: macOS  
Installation: source checkout  
Edit format: search/replace  
Model: not applicable; reproduced by directly invoking deterministic filename parsing code

unique_issues.title: Benchmark scores an exercise as solved based on a test command exit code that the model's own files control
unique_issues.body:
# Benchmark scores an exercise as solved based on a test command exit code that the model's own files control

Affected: Aider-AI/aider@5dc9490

## Summary

`run_unit_tests` decides whether an exercise was solved solely from the exit
code of a test command executed with `cwd=testdir`
(benchmark/benchmark.py:1027-1038). The testdir is the model-writable working
tree, and the benchmark harness auto-approves creation of new files (and
edits to existing files that were not added to the chat), so a response can
plant a file that forces the exit code to 0. A four line `conftest.py` makes
pytest exit 0 while every test fails, and the exercise is recorded with
`tests_outcomes: [true]` (benchmark/benchmark.py:889-893) and counts toward
`pass_rate_1`/`pass_rate_2` on the leaderboard.

The same primitive reaches the other languages because their runner config
files live in the exercise directory: `package.json` for JavaScript
(benchmark/npm-test.sh:12 runs `npm run test`), `CMakeLists.txt` for C++,
`build.gradle` for Java, `Cargo.toml` for Rust. Test files themselves are
restored from the pristine copy before each attempt
(benchmark/benchmark.py:1007-1014), but none of these runner config files
are.

## Why the harness auto-approves the payload

- The benchmark creates `InputOutput(pretty=False, yes=True, ...)`
  (benchmark/benchmark.py:786-790).
- With `yes is True`, `confirm_ask` returns "y" without asking
  (aider/io.py:866-867).
- `allowed_to_edit` asks "Create new file?" for a path that does not exist
  (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2206-2224) and "Allow edits to file that has
  not been added to the chat?" for one that does
  (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2226-2240). Both are auto-approved.

The docker warning (benchmark/benchmark.py:252-254) is about the safety of
running unvetted code on the host. It does not cover this: the score itself
is what is compromised, and a gamed run is indistinguishable from an honest
one in the results yaml and on the leaderboard, which accepts
community-submitted results (benchmark/README.md,
aider/website/docs/leaderboards/contrib.md).

## Reproduction

The PoC vendors `run_unit_tests` and the try-loop decision verbatim from
benchmark/benchmark.py (lines 981-1049 and 889-893) and runs them on a
fabricated python exercise (leap year) whose solution file is deliberately
wrong in both arms. The only difference between the arms is a
model-creatable `conftest.py`.

```
python3 -m pip install --target /tmp/aider-poc-deps pytest
R8E2_DEPS=/tmp/aider-poc-deps python3 poc_f1_grader_exit_code.py f1-evidence.json
```

(`R8E2_DEPS` is only used to put a working `pytest` on PATH, mirroring the
benchmark container. Any environment with `pytest` importable works.)

Observed (evidence file, deterministic across runs):

- control arm: wrong implementation, no conftest: pytest exit code 1,
  failure output returned, benchmark records outcome `False`
- conftest arm: the identical wrong implementation plus this `conftest.py`:

  ```
  def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):
      if exitstatus != 0:
          session.exitstatus = 0
  ```

  pytest exit code 0, `run_unit_tests` returns None, benchmark records
  outcome `True`, i.e. solved. The chat history still contains the FAILED
  test lines while the exercise is scored solved.

The PoC asserts the implementation file is byte-identical between the arms,
so the flip is attributable to the exit-code channel alone.

## Impact

- Any model that emits a `conftest.py` (or rewrites `package.json`,
  `CMakeLists.txt`, `build.gradle`) converts every failing exercise of that
  language into a solved one. On the 225 exercise polyglot set this is a
  path to an arbitrary leaderboard score without solving any task.
- The python arm and the approval chain are executed/proved at the pin; the
  JavaScript/C++/Java/Rust arms follow from the same approval chain plus the
  runner config files being model-editable and not restored, but were not
  executed here.
- It also silently invalidates cross-model comparisons: a run is recorded
  with the same `model`, `edit_format` and cost fields as an honest one.

## Suggestions

- Restore the whole exercise directory from the pristine copy before each
  test attempt, except the specific solution files the model was given, so
  no model-created artifact can influence the test run.
- Or run the tests in a scratch copy containing only the restored test files
  plus the solution files, with an explicit pytest config
  (`-c`, `-p no:cacheprovider`, fixed `--rootdir`) so no in-tree conftest or
  ini file is picked up.
- Additionally parse the test output for the pass/fail summary instead of
  trusting the exit code alone, and treat a 0-exit run whose summary shows
  failures as a harness error rather than a solved exercise.

unique_issues.title: A valid multi-file edit is silently discarded if the response merely mentions an unrelated existing file (whole/editor-whole formats, non-interactive --yes-always)
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

## Environment

- aider 0.86.2
- Python 3.12.11
- Reproduced with a local OpenAI-compatible model (llama.cpp server) as the editor model in `--architect` mode, `--editor-edit-format editor-whole`, `--yes-always`, `--no-show-model-warnings`. Also reasoned through and confirmed to apply to the `whole` edit format directly (not just the `--architect`/`editor-whole` combination).

## Summary

When a model's response is otherwise a perfectly valid `whole`/`editor-whole` edit, but the response text *also happens to contain*, anywhere, a string that matches the relative path or unique basename of some other file in the repo, `check_for_file_mentions()` treats that as an implicit request to add the file to the chat. Under `--yes-always` this is auto-confirmed, and the **entire current response is discarded** (via `reflected_message`) before `apply_updates()` is ever called — including the edits that had nothing to do with the mentioned file. In the worst case (many mentions at once) this triggers a token-limit crash on the next turn and the session ends having applied nothing at all, including the parts of the response that were completely correct.

This is not a model-quality problem: the model can behave perfectly and still lose its own valid edit, because the file-mention detection is a naive whole-text-token scan with no way to distinguish "this filename appears because it's part of the normal, unchanged content of a file I'm dutifully reproducing in full" from "I am asking for this file's content."

## Minimal reproduction (no LLM required — pure text-matching bug)

The core issue is fully deterministic and reproducible without ever calling a model, by exercising `get_file_mentions()` directly against a toy repo:

```python
from aider.coders.base_coder import Coder
from aider.io import InputOutput
from aider.models import Model

# any repo with at least: Makefile, src/foo.c, include/bar.h, include/sub/baz.h
io = InputOutput(yes=True)
model = Model("gpt-4o")  # never actually called
coder = Coder.create(main_model=model, io=io, fnames=[], use_git=True)

# (1) A line that would appear, unchanged, in a Makefile rule for a
#     *different* target than the one being edited:
print(coder.get_file_mentions("cc -o out src/foo.c\n"))
# -> {'src/foo.c'}   (matches: exact repo-root-relative path)

# (2) A flat #include of a top-level header, in a .c file whose *own* edit
#     has nothing to do with bar.h:
print(coder.get_file_mentions('#include "bar.h"\n'))
# -> {'include/bar.h'}   (matches: unique basename)

# (3) The same header, but included via a subdirectory-relative path
#     (relative to the compiler's -I search path, not the repo root):
print(coder.get_file_mentions('#include "sub/baz.h"\n'))
# -> set()   (neither strategy matches - this one "accidentally" escapes)
```

Case (1) and (2) both register a "mention" purely because the string happens to be present, with zero regard for *why* it's present. In a real editing session, (1) and (2) are exactly what happens whenever a model reproduces, in full, a file that has pre-existing references to other files it was never asked to touch (a Makefile with several build targets, a source file with several `#include`s of top-level headers, a CMakeLists.txt listing other sources, an `__init__.py` re-exporting other modules, etc.).

## Real-world consequence

1. User asks for 3 things: edit `include/bar.h`, create a new test file, add a target to `Makefile`.
2. The editor model does all 3 correctly. Because it's rewriting the *whole* Makefile (required by `whole`/`editor-whole`), the unchanged parts of the Makefile still contain build-dependency lines naming several other pre-existing source files.
3. `check_for_file_mentions()` on the model's own response (`base_coder.py`, `check_for_file_mentions` at line 1761, called from `send_message`'s tail around line 1561-1566) picks up every one of those pre-existing filenames.
4. Under `--yes-always`, `confirm_ask("Add file to the chat?", ...)` (`io.py`, `if self.yes is True: res = "y"` around line 866/940) auto-confirms adding *all* of them, with no cap.
5. Back in `run_one` (`base_coder.py`), `reflected_message` is set and the function returns *before* `apply_updates()` is reached — the correct edit for all 3 originally-requested files is thrown away, and a new turn starts with all those extra files now injected as full content.
6. If the model responds to *that* turn by (reasonably, given its system prompt: `wholefile_prompts.py`'s `system_reminder` literally says "Output a copy of each file that needs changes") producing content for some of those newly-injected files too, the cycle can repeat and blow through the model's context window well before `max_reflections` (default 3, `base_coder.py:101`) is ever reached. The session then ends having applied **nothing**: not the newly-requested edits, not the incidentally-fetched files, nothing.

We verified this end-to-end with a real (small, local) model: a 3-file task that the model completed correctly on its first attempt still resulted in zero applied edits and zero commits, twice, purely because of this mechanism.

## Why `--yes-always` makes it worse, but doesn't cause it

Note that `check_for_file_mentions()` only runs on the *editor's own generated reply* in the `--architect`/`auto_accept_architect` flow, because `ArchitectCoder.reply_completed()` calls `editor_coder.run(with_message=content, preproc=False)` (`architect_coder.py:44`) — `preproc=False` skips scanning the *incoming* instruction for mentions. So the *only* place this fires is on the editor's own output, and it is also the *only* mechanism by which the editor model can legitimately obtain the content of a pre-existing file it needs to edit but wasn't given up front. This means a blanket "never auto-confirm" patch (e.g. forcing `explicit_yes_required=True` on that one `confirm_ask` call) is not a safe fix — it would break the common, legitimate case (editor mentions a file it genuinely needs) along with the pathological one.

## Suggested directions

1. **Apply first, reflect second.** Reorder so `apply_updates()` runs on the *current* response before `check_for_file_mentions()` can short-circuit it. A response that contains valid, applicable edits should never be discarded wholesale just because it *also* mentions an unrelated file elsewhere in its text. Any genuinely-needed file could still be fetched for a *following* turn, without cost to the edits that already succeeded. This seems like the smallest, safest change and would have prevented 100% of what we observed.
2. **Cap the blast radius per turn.** If a single response newly mentions more than some small N files (e.g. 2-3) at once, treat it as noise rather than genuine intent and don't add any of them / don't reflect. A real, deliberate "I need file X" request is almost always one file, not a dozen.
3. **An explicit, unambiguous protocol** for the editor to request a file's content (e.g. a distinct marker like `FILE-REQUEST(path)`) instead of inferring intent from incidental text matching. This is the most robust fix but also the most invasive (changes the contract with every edit-format's system prompt).
4. At minimum, **document this failure mode** for anyone running aider non-interactively (`--yes-always`, CI/agentic pipelines): whole-file reproduction of any file that itself references other project files (build files, `__init__.py`, headers with flat includes, etc.) is currently unsafe and can silently discard otherwise-correct multi-file edits.

Happy to share the full verbose logs of his issue if usefu and hope this info could help!

_No response_

unique_issues.title: Add a Hook System for Extensible Automation
unique_issues.body:
Add a hook system that lets users run custom commands or scripts at key points in the workflow. For example before/after an AI edit, before a commit, after tests, or when a command fails.
This would make the tool easier to integrate with existing development workflows without requiring core changes for every use case.
Suggested capabilities
- Configurable lifecycle events, such as:
  - pre_edit / post_edit
  - pre_commit / post_commit
  - pre_test / post_test
  - on_error
- Project-level configuration, with optional user-level defaults.
- Hooks defined as shell commands or executable scripts.
- Access to structured context through environment variables or JSON stdin (changed files, command result, exit code, etc.).
- Clear output and failure behavior, including an option for a hook failure to block the next step.
Example
```yaml
hooks:
  post_edit:
    - command: npm run lint
    - command: npm test
      blocking: true

  pre_commit:
    - command: prettier --write $CHANGED_FILES
```
Acceptance criteria
- Users can configure one or more commands for supported lifecycle events.
- Hooks receive useful execution context.
- Hook output and failures are visible and understandable.
- Blocking vs. non-blocking behavior is configurable.
- Documentation includes the event list, configuration schema, and examples.

unique_issues.title: Benchmark records an exercise as solved when the test command exits non-zero with no output
unique_issues.body:
`benchmark/benchmark.py:1038-1048` (`run_unit_tests`, defined at `:981`), read by its caller at `:881-892`; solved exercises are counted at `:508`. Code as of 5dc9490 (current `main`).

```python
    success = result.returncode == 0
    res = result.stdout
    res = cleanup_test_output(res, testdir)
    ...
    if not success:
        print(f"Tests failed: {testdir}")
        return res
```

```python
        try:
            errors = run_unit_tests(original_dname, testdir, history_fname, test_files)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            errors = "Tests timed out!"
            timeouts += 1

        if errors:
            test_outcomes.append(False)
        else:
            test_outcomes.append(True)
            break
```

`run_unit_tests` reports a failing run by returning the runner's output and a passing run by returning `None`. The return code decides only whether that text is returned; the caller then decides pass or fail from whether the text is non-empty. A test command that exits non-zero with empty output returns `""`, so the exercise is recorded as solved (`test_outcomes.append(True)`) straight after the function has printed "Tests failed".

Stderr is merged into stdout (`stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`, `:1030`), so this needs a process that dies before it writes anything. With pytest that happens when the process is killed, or exits through `os._exit`, before collection finishes, for example while importing the solution module: the header has not been flushed yet. A process that dies inside a test, after collection, has already written its header and is scored correctly.

## Measured

Method: `run_unit_tests` and `cleanup_test_output` were extracted with `ast` from 5dc9490 and executed in a plain Python process, and the caller's `if errors:` test was applied to the return value. `pytest` on `PATH` was a shim that runs `python -m pytest` (pytest 9.1.1, Python 3.12.4). The `dump` helper was replaced with a no-op. `benchmark.py` itself was not run, and no exercise was run through a model.

| Case | Returned | Recorded | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| control: solution wrong, one failing test | runner output | failed | failed |
| control: solution right | `None` | passed | passed |
| solution kills its own process with SIGKILL while pytest imports it | `""` | **passed** | failed |
| solution calls `os._exit(1)` while pytest imports it | `""` | **passed** | failed |
| control: process killed inside a test, after collection | runner output | failed | failed |

Not measured: how often a real run ends a test process with no output (for example an out-of-memory kill during import), and the other runners in `TEST_COMMANDS` (`cargo`, `go`, `gradlew`, `npm-test.sh`, `cpp-test.sh`), which were not run.

## Consequence

An exercise whose test process dies before printing anything is counted in `pass_rate_1` / `pass_rate_2` (`:508-513`) as solved. `benchmark/README.md:125-126` defines those figures as the percent of tasks that had all tests passing, and the README invites benchmark results to be submitted for the leaderboard data files (`:143-144`).

Related, with a different mechanism: #5681 and #5688 (a model-created `conftest.py` that makes the runner exit 0 while tests fail). That change distrusts an exit code of 0; the `if not success: return res` path above is not touched by it.

## Suggested fix

The same function already computes `success = result.returncode == 0` (`:1038`). Return a non-empty message whenever `not success`, for example `return res or f"Tests failed with exit code {result.returncode}"`, so the caller's truthiness test can no longer read a failure as a pass.

unique_issues.title: Security : an edit format can write and delete files outside the repository root, bypassing the edit-confirmation prompt
unique_issues.body:
I'd like to report a security vulnerability in aider **privately** (currently unpatched). This repo has no `SECURITY.md` and GitHub **private vulnerability reporting** is not enabled, so there is no private channel to send details to.

**Please either** enable **Settings → Advanced Security → Private vulnerability reporting**, or share a security contact (email). I'll then send the full write-up, a one-command reproduction, CVSS, and a proposed patch.

**High level only (no specifics here):** in one of aider's edit formats, a file operation can be steered to a destination outside the repository root. That destination is neither confined to the repo nor surfaced by the edit-confirmation prompt users rely on, so aider can create/overwrite a file anywhere the process can write — and delete the in-repo original — with no prompt. Because the written content and path are model-controlled and aider routinely feeds untrusted text to the model, this allows writing to sensitive locations and, in turn, code execution. Assessed **High** severity (path traversal + confirmation bypass).

Reproduced against current `main`. Happy to follow a 90-day coordinated-disclosure timeline. Filing a separate issue for another, unrelated finding.

Thanks!

unique_issues.title: Question/proposal: compiler-backed repo context for Semaprax .spx files
unique_issues.body:
### Issue
Aider's repo map and edit formats work well for text-oriented workflows. For Semaprax `.spx`, the compiler can answer a narrower question: which declaration has a stable `@id`, what are its contracts and callers, and whether a proposed semantic patch still targets the source revision the agent inspected. I would like an opt-in Semaprax mode that feeds bounded compiler context into Aider and applies supported semantic edits through the compiler's checked patch route.

The first slice could be a rename across a small `.spx` project. It would show the relevant semantic neighborhood instead of a whole graph, preview affected declarations, and refuse a stale apply. Ordinary text edits could remain available for unsupported operations, followed by `semaprax check` through Aider's existing `--lint-cmd` path. This is a request for a narrow integration experiment, not a claim that Aider currently understands Semaprax syntax.

Would a language-specific context/edit provider belong in Aider, or should this be kept as an external wrapper? A tiny fixture and comparison with the current repo-map path could answer whether it improves precision and token use.

unique_issues.title: Docs: verifying browser flows in the --auto-test loop
unique_issues.body:
Disclosure up front: I work at TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) and we build the tools below. Raising this as an issue rather than a PR so you can say no before anyone writes anything.

**The gap**

`--auto-test` with `--test-cmd` is a good loop: aider edits, the suite runs, and aider fixes what it broke. But for anything with a web UI, a green unit suite does not mean the flow still works in a browser. Aider can make the tests pass and still leave the page broken, and nothing in the loop catches that.

**This already works, with no changes to aider**

Kane CLI takes a flow described in natural language, drives real Chrome, and exits 0 on pass, 1 on fail, 2 on an auth or setup error, and 3 on timeout. Your docs say aider treats a non-zero exit from the test command as errors to fix, so Kane CLI fits the existing loop. After a one-time `kane-cli login`:

```
aider --auto-test --test-cmd 'kane-cli run "Go to http://localhost:3000, add the first item to the cart, and verify the cart badge shows 1" --agent --headless'
```

`--agent` switches Kane CLI to non-interactive NDJSON output, so it does not stop to ask questions inside aider's terminal. `--headless` keeps Chrome off screen. When the flow fails, aider offers to fix it, with the usual limit of three attempts. Every run also leaves a replayable .evidence pack with screenshots, network and console logs.

One caveat a docs page would need: exit codes 2 and 3 are also non-zero, so if you are not signed in or the dev server is down, aider will try to fix code that is not broken. The page would say to run `kane-cli login` and start the app first. Kane CLI needs a TestMu AI account.

https://github.com/LambdaTest/kane-cli · docs: https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-quickstart

**The ask**

Would you take a short docs page under Usage, something like "browser testing in the edit-test loop", showing this pattern? Happy to write it. If you would rather not carry a third-party tool in the docs, that is a fair answer and I will leave it.

**Two others, mentioned only because they are adjacent**

Browser Cloud runs Chrome sessions in the cloud with parallelism and session persistence, which matters if that test command runs in CI rather than on a laptop. https://www.testmuai.com/browser-cloud/

Rook CLI grades what an AI agent actually changed rather than what it reports doing. It is aimed at people building agents, so it is more relevant to aider's own development than to aider's users. Apache-2.0, pre-alpha. https://www.testmuai.com/rook-cli/

unique_issues.title: BUG: unreadable `--message-file` (missing path or directory) drops into interactive chat and exits 0 instead of failing
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

## Summary

When the file given to `--message-file` cannot be read (it does not exist, or it is a directory), aider prints an error, then enters the interactive chat loop instead of exiting, and finally exits with status 0. `main()` has `except FileNotFoundError` / `except IOError` handlers that print "Message file not found" / "Error reading message file" and `return 1`, but they never run: `io.read_text()` already catches these errors and returns `None`, and `coder.run(with_message=None)` starts the chat loop.

In automation this means a wrong path reads further commands from stdin (or waits on a terminal) and reports success.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` (no API key or network needed; no message reaches a model).
2. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
# An unreadable --message-file does not fail: aider enters interactive chat and exits 0.
# Requires only `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0`; no API key or network (no message reaches a model).
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import aider

print("aider", aider.__version__)

# the console script installed next to this interpreter (or on PATH)
aider_cmd = shutil.which("aider", path=str(Path(sys.executable).parent)) or shutil.which("aider")
cwd = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(cwd / "a_directory").mkdir()
env = dict(os.environ, OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-dummy")
opts = ["--model", "gpt-4o", "--no-git", "--no-check-update", "--no-analytics",
        "--no-show-release-notes", "--no-show-model-warnings", "--no-fancy-input", "--no-pretty"]

for message_file in ["missing.txt", "a_directory"]:
    # stdin holds one line, as if typed at the chat prompt
    proc = subprocess.run([aider_cmd, *opts, "--message-file", message_file], cwd=cwd, env=env,
                          input="/ls\n", capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    print(f"$ echo /ls | aider --message-file {message_file} ...")
    print(proc.stdout.strip())
    print(f"exit status: {proc.returncode}\n")
```

3. Run `python repro.py`.

## Actual output

```text
aider 0.86.0
$ echo /ls | aider --message-file missing.txt ...
Aider v0.86.0
Main model: gpt-4o with diff edit format
Weak model: gpt-4o-mini
Git repo: none
Repo-map: disabled
missing.txt: file not found error


> 

No files in chat, git repo, or read-only list.

>
exit status: 0

$ echo /ls | aider --message-file a_directory ...
Aider v0.86.0
Main model: gpt-4o with diff edit format
Weak model: gpt-4o-mini
Git repo: none
Repo-map: disabled
a_directory: is a directory


> 

No files in chat, git repo, or read-only list.

>
exit status: 0
```

The `/ls` line on stdin is executed at the interactive `>` prompt. `main` at `5dc9490b` prints the same (only the version lines differ).

## Expected behavior

Aider reports the unreadable message file and exits with status 1, without entering chat mode.

- `--message-file` is documented as "Specify a file containing the message to send the LLM, process reply, then exit (disables chat mode)" ([options.md L617-L618](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/website/docs/config/options.md#L617-L618)).
- `main()` already defines this outcome: "Message file not found" / "Error reading message file" followed by `return 1` ([`main.py` L1136-L1151](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/main.py#L1136-L1151)).

## Root cause

```python
if args.message_file:
    try:
        message_from_file = io.read_text(args.message_file)
        io.tool_output()
        coder.run(with_message=message_from_file)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        io.tool_error(f"Message file not found: {args.message_file}")
        ...
        return 1
    except IOError as e:
        ...
        return 1
```

1. `InputOutput.read_text()` catches `FileNotFoundError`, `IsADirectoryError`, `OSError` and `UnicodeError`, prints its own error and returns `None` ([`io.py` L453-L476](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/io.py#L453-L476)), so the `except` branches in `main()` are unreachable.
2. `Coder.run(with_message=None)` treats a falsy message as "no message" and enters the `while True: ... self.get_input()` chat loop ([`base_coder.py` L876-L892](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L876-L892)).
3. When stdin ends, `run()` returns and `main()` reaches `return` (exit 0).

An empty message file takes the same path (`with_message=""`), entering chat without any error message.

## Possible fix direction

Check the result of `read_text()` in the `--message-file` branch and `return 1` when it is `None` (the error has already been printed by `read_text()`); an empty file could get the same treatment or a warning.



### Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.0` (PyPI) and `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` (`0.86.3.dev0`)
Command: `aider --model gpt-4o --no-git --no-fancy-input --no-pretty --message-file <missing file | directory>` (no model call)
Python: `3.12.13`
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

### Issue

## Summary

`InputOutput._validate_color_settings()` handles an invalid `assistant_output_color` by warning "Disabling this color." and setting the attribute to `None`. The assistant reply is then rendered with `rich.markdown.Markdown(..., style=None)`, and Rich raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip'`. With pretty output (the default in a terminal), every reply fails this way, streaming or not, and the edits in the reply are never applied.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` (no API key or network needed; litellm's `mock_response` supplies the reply).
2. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
# An invalid assistant_output_color is "disabled" to None, then every pretty reply crashes in Rich
# and the reply's edit is not applied.
# Requires only `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0`; no API key or network
# (litellm's mock_response supplies the model reply).
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from aider import __version__
from aider.coders import Coder
from aider.io import InputOutput
from aider.models import Model

print("aider", __version__)


def attempt(color):
    os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    Path("greeting.txt").write_text("hello\n")
    model = Model("gpt-4o")
    model.extra_params = {"mock_response": "greeting.txt\n```\ngoodbye\n```\n"}

    coder.run(with_message="Change hello to goodbye.")
    print(f"=== greeting.txt now contains {Path('greeting.txt').read_text()!r}\n")


attempt("#0088ff")  # the CLI default
attempt("not-a-color")
```

```text
=== greeting.txt now contains 'hello\n'
```

With `stream=False` the same `AttributeError` comes from `InputOutput.assistant_output()` instead of the markdown stream. `main` at `5dc9490b` (with rich 14.3.3) prints the same output.

The command line behaves the same way in a terminal, e.g. `aider --assistant-output-color not-a-color --message hi` (model mocked through a `--model-settings-file` with `extra_params: {mock_response: "Hello there."}`):

```text
Warning: Invalid configuration for assistant_output_color: 'not-a-color'. 
'not-a-color' is not a valid color. Disabling this color.
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Aider v0.86.0
Model: gpt-4o with whole edit format
Git repo: none
Repo-map: disabled

░█  Traceback (most recent call last):
...
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip'

'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip'
```

## Expected behavior

After the warning, aider keeps working with the assistant color disabled: replies are rendered (default style) and their edits are applied, as they are with a valid color.

- The warning itself promises a graceful fallback: "Disabling this color." ([`io.py` L374-L398](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/io.py#L374-L398)).
- The other colors that the same method can reset to `None` are only applied when set: `if self.tool_output_color:` in `tool_output` ([`io.py` L1005-L1008](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/io.py#L1005-L1008)) and `style = dict(style=color) if self.pretty and color else dict()` in `_tool_message` ([`io.py` L978](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/io.py#L978)).
- `--assistant-output-color` is a documented option ([options.md L346-L347](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/website/docs/config/options.md#L346-L347)).

## Root cause

1. `_validate_color_settings()` sets an invalid `assistant_output_color` to `None` ([`io.py` L387-L398](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/io.py#L387-L398)).
2. Both reply renderers pass it to Rich unconditionally: `get_assistant_mdstream()` uses `mdargs = dict(style=self.assistant_output_color, ...)` ([`io.py` L1014-L1021](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/io.py#L1014-L1021)) and `assistant_output()` builds `Markdown(message, style=self.assistant_output_color, ...)` ([`io.py` L1034-L1037](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/io.py#L1034-L1037)).
3. `rich.markdown.Markdown` expects a style string (its default is `"none"`); `Console.get_style(None)` calls `Style.parse(None)`, which raises `AttributeError`.
4. `Coder.send_message` catches the exception, prints it and returns ([`base_coder.py` L1506-L1512](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L1506-L1512)), so `apply_updates` never runs for that reply.

## Possible fix direction

Pass `style=self.assistant_output_color or "none"` in both places, or have `_validate_color_settings()` fall back to the default color for `assistant_output_color` instead of `None`.




### Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.0` (PyPI) and `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` (`0.86.3.dev0`)
Switches: `--assistant-output-color not-a-color` (Python API: `InputOutput(pretty=True, assistant_output_color="not-a-color")`)
Model: `gpt-4o` with litellm `mock_response` (no real model call); edit format `whole`
Python: `3.12.13`
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
rich: `14.1.0` (0.86.0) / `14.3.3` (main)

unique_issues.title: BUG: `/undo` never sends `undo_command_reply` to the model because `cmd_undo` discards `raw_cmd_undo`'s return value
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

## Summary

For models with `send_undo_reply: true`, `raw_cmd_undo` returns `prompts.undo_command_reply` so that the model is told its last change was reverted. `cmd_undo` calls `raw_cmd_undo(args)` without returning the result, so the reply is never sent. After `/undo` the model is not told about the revert, and its chat history still describes the reverted edit as applied.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` (git required; no API key or network needed, litellm's `mock_response` supplies the replies).
2. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
# /undo never sends the undo acknowledgement to the model, even with send_undo_reply enabled.
# Requires only `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` and git; no API key or network
# (litellm's mock_response supplies the model replies).
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from aider import __version__, prompts
from aider.coders import Coder
from aider.io import InputOutput
from aider.models import Model

os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
print("aider", __version__)


def git(*args):
    subprocess.run(["git", *args], check=True)


git("init", "-q")
git("config", "user.name", "Example")
git("config", "user.email", "example@example.com")
git("config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
Path("app.py").write_text("VALUE = 1\n")
git("add", "app.py")
git("commit", "-qm", "initial")

model = Model("gpt-4o")
model.send_undo_reply = True  # documented model setting; see adv-model-settings
model.extra_params = {"mock_response": "app.py\n```\nVALUE = 2\n```\n"}
model.weak_model.extra_params = {"mock_response": "Set VALUE to 2"}  # commit message

requests = []  # last message of every request sent to the main model
send_completion = model.send_completion


def counting_send_completion(messages, *args, **kwargs):
    requests.append(messages[-1]["content"])
    return send_completion(messages, *args, **kwargs)


model.send_completion = counting_send_completion

coder = Coder.create(
    main_model=model,
    edit_format="whole",
    io=InputOutput(yes=True, pretty=False, fancy_input=False),
    fnames=["app.py"],
    stream=False,
)
coder.run(with_message="Set VALUE to 2")
print("--- requests to the main model after the edit:", len(requests))

coder.run(with_message="/undo")
print("--- requests to the main model after /undo:", len(requests))
print("undo_command_reply sent:", any(prompts.undo_command_reply in str(r) for r in requests))
print("raw_cmd_undo would have returned it:", repr(prompts.undo_command_reply[:60] + "..."))
```

3. Run `python repro.py`.

## Actual output

````text
aider 0.86.0
app.py

```diff
@@ -1 +1 @@
-VALUE = 1
+VALUE = 2
```


Tokens: 10 sent, 20 received. Cost: $0.00023 message, $0.00023 session.
Applied edit to app.py
Commit fff0364 Set VALUE to 2
--- requests to the main model after the edit: 1
Removed: fff0364 Set VALUE to 2
Now at:  8b7397f initial
--- requests to the main model after /undo: 1
undo_command_reply sent: False
raw_cmd_undo would have returned it: 'I did `git reset --hard HEAD~1` to discard the last edits. P...'
````

`main` at `5dc9490b` prints the same (only the version line and commit hashes differ).

## Expected behavior

With `send_undo_reply` enabled, `/undo` sends `prompts.undo_command_reply` to the model, as a second request in the script above.

- `send_undo_reply` is a documented model setting ([`adv-model-settings.md` L143](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/website/docs/config/adv-model-settings.md#L143), [`models.py` L134](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/models.py#L134)), and Aider's generic settings turn it on for llama-3-70b, gpt-4-turbo/preview and gpt-4/claude-3-opus model names ([`models.py` L508-L525](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/models.py#L508-L525)).
- `raw_cmd_undo` ends with `if self.coder.main_model.send_undo_reply: return prompts.undo_command_reply` ([`commands.py` L654-L655](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/commands.py#L654-L655)).
- A string returned by a command is forwarded as the next message: `Commands.do_run` returns the command's value ([`commands.py` L295-L296](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/commands.py#L295-L296)) and `Coder.run_one` sends whatever `preproc_user_input` returns ([`base_coder.py` L927-L934](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L927-L934)).

The reply asks the model to wait for instructions instead of retrying the reverted change; its wording was added in response to #450 ("/undo immediately re-executes the prior command").

## Root cause

`cmd_undo` drops the return value ([`commands.py` L553-L558](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/commands.py#L553-L558)):

```python
def cmd_undo(self, args):
    "Undo the last git commit if it was done by aider"
    try:
        self.raw_cmd_undo(args)
    except ANY_GIT_ERROR as err:
        self.io.tool_error(f"Unable to complete undo: {err}")
```

This started when the undo body was moved into `raw_cmd_undo` behind a try/except wrapper (8609594c, "refactor: split cmd_undo and cmd_commit into raw and exception-handling methods", v0.55.0).

## Possible fix direction

```python
try:
    return self.raw_cmd_undo(args)
```

Once the reply is sent again, its wording matters: it says `git reset --hard HEAD~1`, while `raw_cmd_undo` checks out the commit's files from `HEAD~1` and then runs `git reset --soft HEAD~1`; PR #4928 proposes updated wording.



### Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.0` (PyPI) and `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` (`0.86.3.dev0`)
Model: `gpt-4o` with `send_undo_reply = True` and litellm `mock_response` (no real model call); weak model `gpt-4o-mini` mocked for the commit message
Edit format: `whole`; git repo with auto-commits on
Python: `3.12.13`
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

unique_issues.title: BUG: `patch` edit format cannot create new files: `*** Add File` fails with "File already exists" and leaves an empty file
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

## Summary

With `--edit-format patch`, a reply that creates a new file with `*** Add File: <path>` is always rejected with `ADD Error: File already exists: <path>`, and an empty file is left behind at that path. The patch system prompt tells the model to use exactly this marker for new files, so the `patch` format cannot create files at all.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` (no API key or network needed; litellm's `mock_response` supplies the reply).
2. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
# patch edit format: "*** Add File" cannot create a new file.
# Requires only `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0`; no API key or network
# (litellm's mock_response supplies the model reply).
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from aider import __version__
from aider.coders import Coder
from aider.io import InputOutput
from aider.models import Model

os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
print("aider", __version__)

reply = """*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.py
+def hello():
+    print("hello")
*** End Patch
"""

model = Model("gpt-4o")
model.extra_params = {"mock_response": reply}
coder = Coder.create(
    main_model=model,
    edit_format="patch",
    io=InputOutput(yes=True, pretty=False, fancy_input=False),
    use_git=False,
    stream=False,
)
coder.max_reflections = 0  # one attempt is enough to show the failure
coder.run(with_message="Create hello.py with a hello() function.")

path = Path("hello.py")
print("---")
print("hello.py exists:", path.exists())
print("hello.py content:", repr(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else None)
```

3. Run `python repro.py`.

## Actual output

```text
aider 0.86.0
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.py
+def hello():
+    print("hello")
*** End Patch

Tokens: 10 sent, 20 received. Cost: $0.00023 message, $0.00023 session.

hello.py
The LLM did not conform to the edit format.
https://aider.chat/docs/troubleshooting/edit-errors.html

Error applying action 'ActionType.ADD' to hello.py: ADD Error: File already 
exists: hello.py
Only 0 reflections allowed, stopping.
---
hello.py exists: True
hello.py content: ''
```

`main` at `5dc9490b` prints the same output (only the version line differs). With the default `max_reflections`, every retry fails the same way, because the empty file from the first attempt is still there.

## Expected behavior

`hello.py` is created with the two lines from the patch.

The `patch` system prompt asks for this format when the model creates a file:

- [`aider/coders/patch_prompts.py` L153](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/patch_prompts.py#L153): "For `Add` actions, use the `*** Add File: [path/to/new/file]` marker, followed by the lines of the new file, each preceded by a plus sign `+`."
- The worked example in the same prompt creates `hello.py` with `*** Add File: hello.py` ([L95](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/patch_prompts.py#L95)).

The other edit formats create new files through the same `allowed_to_edit` path and then write the new content into the file it creates.

## Root cause

1. `Coder.apply_updates` runs `prepare_to_edit(edits)` before `apply_edits(edits)` ([`base_coder.py` L2296-L2304](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L2296-L2304)).
2. `prepare_to_edit` calls `allowed_to_edit(path)`. For a path that does not exist yet, `allowed_to_edit` confirms "Create new file?" and then calls `utils.touch_file(full_path)`, which creates an empty file ([`base_coder.py` L2206-L2224](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L2206-L2224)). In a git repo the new file is also `git add`ed (on `main`, when auto-commits are on).
3. `PatchCoder.apply_edits` then handles the ADD action by checking `path_obj.exists()` and raising `DiffError("ADD Error: File already exists: ...")` ([`patch_coder.py` L566-L569](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/patch_coder.py#L566-L569)). The file always exists at this point because step 2 just created it.
4. `DiffError` is a `ValueError`, so `apply_updates` reports the reply as malformed and reflects the error to the model. The empty file remains.

## Possible fix direction

Make the ADD check see the file system as it was before `prepare_to_edit`, for example by recording the paths that `allowed_to_edit` touched and letting ADD write to such a path, or by accepting ADD when the target exists and is empty. A regression test that runs a mocked `*** Add File` reply through `Coder.run` would cover the full `apply_updates` sequence.


### Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.0` (PyPI) and `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` (`0.86.3.dev0`)
Edit format: `patch` (`--edit-format patch`)
Model: `gpt-4o` with litellm `mock_response` (no real model call)
Python: `3.12.13`
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
litellm: `1.75.0` (0.86.0) / `1.82.3` (main)

unique_issues.title: BUG: callable `test_cmd` crashes `Coder.get_platform_info` with `TypeError` on the first message
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

## Summary

`Commands.cmd_test` supports a callable test command (`test_cmd`), and `Coder.create(..., test_cmd=...)` accepts one. But `Coder.get_platform_info()` builds the system prompt with `self.test_cmd + "\n"`, so any coder whose `test_cmd` is a callable raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'function' and 'str'` on its first chat message, before the model is called. This happens with or without `auto_test`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` (no API key or network needed; litellm's `mock_response` supplies the reply).
2. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
# A callable test_cmd (supported by Commands.cmd_test) crashes the first chat message.
# Requires only `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0`; no API key or network
# (litellm's mock_response supplies the model reply).
import os
import tempfile

from aider import __version__
from aider.coders import Coder
from aider.io import InputOutput
from aider.models import Model

os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
print("aider", __version__)


def run_tests():
    return "1 test failed"  # a callable test command returns its error output


model = Model("gpt-4o")
model.extra_params = {"mock_response": "Ok."}
coder = Coder.create(
    main_model=model,
    edit_format="whole",
    io=InputOutput(yes=True, pretty=False, fancy_input=False),
    use_git=False,
    stream=False,
    test_cmd=run_tests,
)

print("/test with the callable test_cmd returns:", repr(coder.commands.cmd_test("")))
print("--- sending a chat message")
coder.run(with_message="Hello")
print("--- reply:", repr(coder.partial_response_content))
```

3. Run `python repro.py`.

## Actual output

(paths shortened)

```text
aider 0.86.0
1 test failed
/test with the callable test_cmd returns: '1 test failed'
--- sending a chat message
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/.../repro.py", line 33, in <module>
    coder.run(with_message="Hello")
  File ".../site-packages/aider/coders/base_coder.py", line 880, in run
    self.run_one(with_message, preproc)
  File ".../site-packages/aider/coders/base_coder.py", line 934, in run_one
    list(self.send_message(message))
  File ".../site-packages/aider/coders/base_coder.py", line 1429, in send_message
    chunks = self.format_messages()
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/aider/coders/base_coder.py", line 1334, in format_messages
    chunks = self.format_chat_chunks()
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/aider/coders/base_coder.py", line 1228, in format_chat_chunks
    main_sys = self.fmt_system_prompt(self.gpt_prompts.main_system)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/aider/coders/base_coder.py", line 1185, in fmt_system_prompt
    platform_text = self.get_platform_info()
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/aider/coders/base_coder.py", line 1170, in get_platform_info
    platform_text += self.test_cmd + "\n"
                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'function' and 'str'
```

`main` at `5dc9490b` fails at the same line with the same traceback.

## Expected behavior

The chat message is sent and answered, and the callable keeps working as the test command (`/test`, and auto-test after edits when `auto_test=True`).

`Commands.cmd_test` explicitly handles a callable `test_cmd`, including when it falls back to `self.coder.test_cmd` ([`commands.py` L993-L1011](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/commands.py#L993-L1011)):

```python
if not args and self.coder.test_cmd:
    args = self.coder.test_cmd
...
if not callable(args):
    if type(args) is not str:
        raise ValueError(repr(args))
    return self.cmd_run(args, True)

errors = args()
```

The first part of the script shows that path working. The auto-test path passes `self.test_cmd` to `cmd_test` unchanged ([`base_coder.py` L1617](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L1617)).

## Root cause

`Coder.get_platform_info()` assumes `test_cmd` is a string ([`base_coder.py` L1163-L1170](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L1163-L1170)):

```python
if self.test_cmd:
    ...
    platform_text += self.test_cmd + "\n"
```

`fmt_system_prompt()` calls `get_platform_info()` for every request, so the `TypeError` is raised while the first message is formatted. Callable test commands were added in 449cbf50 ("Allow test_cmd to be a callable", v0.37.0); the test command was added to the platform info later in 33793ca9 (v0.54.x).

## Possible fix direction

Only add the test command text to the platform info when it is a string (for example `if isinstance(self.test_cmd, str)`), or describe a callable generically (for example its `__name__`).



### Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.0` (PyPI) and `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` (`0.86.3.dev0`)
Usage: Python API (`Coder.create(..., test_cmd=<callable>)`)
Model: `gpt-4o` with litellm `mock_response` (the crash happens before any model call)
Python: `3.12.13`
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

unique_issues.title: BUG: `/code` without arguments summarizes and replaces the chat history, unlike `/chat-mode code`
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

## Summary

Switching back to code mode with `/code` (no arguments) sends the existing chat history to the summarizer model and replaces it with a summary. `/chat-mode code`, which performs the same switch, keeps the history verbatim and makes no extra model call. Commit [1a3466e](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/commit/1a3466e413f4d82a82136506435b48b54f13aa1e) ("do not summarize when switching to code or ask mode") intended the second behavior for both.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` (no network or real model call needed).
2. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
# `/code` (no arguments) summarizes the chat history; `/chat-mode code` does not.
# Requires only `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0`; no real model call (Coder.send and the
# summarizer transport are stubbed). Set OPENAI_API_KEY to any value to silence the key warning.
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

import aider
from aider.coders import Coder
from aider.commands import SwitchCoder
from aider.io import InputOutput
from aider.models import Model

print("aider", aider.__version__, aider.__file__)
root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
os.chdir(root)
run = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", *a], check=True, capture_output=True)  # noqa: E731
run("init", "-q")
run("config", "user.email", "r@example.invalid")
run("config", "user.name", "r")
(root / "quota.py").write_text("LIMIT = 0\n")
run("add", ".")
run("commit", "-qm", "init")

REPLIES = iter([
    "quota.py\n```python\nLIMIT = 5\n```\n",   # code-mode edit (whole format)
    "7 x 6 = 42 bottles.",                     # ask-mode answer
])


def fake_send(self, messages, model=None, functions=None):
    self.partial_response_content = next(REPLIES)
    self.partial_response_function_call = dict()
    return []
    yield


summarizer_calls = []


def fake_simple_send(self, messages):
    summarizer_calls.append(messages)
    return "I asked you to set LIMIT and then asked a question."


def switch(coder, command):
    try:
        coder.commands.run(command)
    except SwitchCoder as sw:
        # same as main.py:1172-1177
        kwargs = dict(io=coder.io, from_coder=coder)
        kwargs.update(sw.kwargs)
        kwargs.pop("show_announcements", None)
        return sw.kwargs, Coder.create(**kwargs)
    raise SystemExit(f"{command} did not raise SwitchCoder")


io = InputOutput(pretty=False, yes=True, fancy_input=False)
with mock.patch.object(Coder, "send", fake_send), \
        mock.patch.object(Model, "simple_send_with_retries", fake_simple_send):
    code = Coder.create(main_model=Model("gpt-4o-mini"), edit_format="whole", io=io,
                        fnames=["quota.py"], stream=False, auto_commits=False, map_tokens=0,
                        suggest_shell_commands=False)
    code.run(with_message="Set LIMIT in quota.py to 5.")
    code.summarizer_thread and code.summarizer_thread.join()
    history = list(code.done_messages)
    print("done_messages after the code-mode edit:", len(history))

    kw_ask, ask = switch(code, "/ask")
    print("/ask         -> SwitchCoder kwargs:", kw_ask, "| summarizer calls:", len(summarizer_calls))
    ask.run(with_message="How many bottles are in 7 cartons of 6?")

    results = {}
    for command in ("/chat-mode code", "/code"):
        before = len(summarizer_calls)
        kw, new = switch(ask, command)
        calls = len(summarizer_calls) - before
        kept = new.done_messages == history
        results[command] = (calls, kept)
        print(f"{command:<15} -> SwitchCoder kwargs: {kw} | edit_format={new.edit_format} | "
              f"summarizer calls: {calls} | done_messages kept verbatim: {kept} | "
              f"first done message: {new.done_messages[0]['content'][:60]!r}")

if results["/chat-mode code"] == (0, True) and results["/code"][0] > 0 and not results["/code"][1]:
    print("RESULT: BUG_REPRODUCED (/code summarizes and replaces the history; /chat-mode code does not)")
else:
    print("RESULT: OK", results)
```

3. Run `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-none python repro.py`.

## Actual output

```text
aider 0.86.0 .../site-packages/aider/__init__.py

Applied edit to quota.py
done_messages after the code-mode edit: 4
/ask         -> SwitchCoder kwargs: {'edit_format': 'ask', 'summarize_from_coder': False} | summarizer calls: 0

/chat-mode code -> SwitchCoder kwargs: {'edit_format': 'whole', 'summarize_from_coder': False} | edit_format=whole | summarizer calls: 0 | done_messages kept verbatim: True | first done message: 'Set LIMIT in quota.py to 5.'
/code           -> SwitchCoder kwargs: {'edit_format': 'whole', 'summarize_from_coder': True} | edit_format=whole | summarizer calls: 1 | done_messages kept verbatim: False | first done message: 'I spoke to you previously about a number of things.\nI asked '
RESULT: BUG_REPRODUCED (/code summarizes and replaces the history; /chat-mode code does not)
```

`main` at `5dc9490b` prints the same (only the version line differs).

## Expected behavior

`/code` should switch back to code mode like `/chat-mode code`: `summarize_from_coder=False`, no summarizer call, and the earlier conversation kept as it was. The docs present the argument-free commands as the way to switch modes ([usage/modes.md](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/website/docs/usage/modes.md#L32-L38)), and `cmd_chat_mode` explicitly disables summarization for the `code` and `ask` targets ([commands.py L191-L198](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/commands.py#L191-L198)).

## Root cause

[`cmd_code`](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/commands.py#L1186-L1188) calls `_generic_chat_command(args, self.coder.main_model.edit_format)`. Without arguments this becomes `cmd_chat_mode("whole")` / `cmd_chat_mode("diff")`, not `cmd_chat_mode("code")`, so the `if ef == "code":` branch that sets `summarize_from_coder = False` is skipped. `Coder.create` then summarizes because the edit format changes ([base_coder.py L161](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L161)). The argument-free switch was added in [1a84c10](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/commit/1a84c109fcb25858c78c39b37873632ca59d015f) after the summarization rule.

## Possible fix direction

Treat an argument-free `/code` as the `code` mode (for example, pass `"code"` to `cmd_chat_mode` when there are no arguments), or set `summarize_from_coder=False` in that path.


### Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.0` (PyPI) and `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` (`0.86.3.dev0`)
Model: `gpt-4o-mini` with `Coder.send` and the summarizer transport stubbed (no real model call)
Edit format: `whole`
Python: `3.12.13`
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

unique_issues.title: BUG: a failed file write is reported to the model as "I updated the files." and counted as an edit
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

## Summary

When writing an edit to disk fails with an `OSError` (for example `PermissionError` on a read-only file), Aider prints the write error but then treats the file as edited: it adds the path to `aider_edited_files` and appends "I updated the files." / "Ok." to the chat history. The file on disk is unchanged, so the next turn tells the model that an edit was applied when it was not. No reflection is sent, so the model gets no chance to react to the failure.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0` (no API key or network needed; the model reply is scripted).
2. Save as `repro.py`:

```python
# A failed write is reported to the model as "I updated the files." and counted as an edit.
# Requires only `pip install aider-chat==0.86.0`; no API key or network (litellm.completion is scripted).
import os
import stat
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import litellm

import aider
from aider.coders import Coder
from aider.io import InputOutput
from aider.models import Model

print("aider", aider.__version__)


def completion(**kwargs):
    return litellm.ModelResponse(
        model=kwargs["model"],
        choices=[{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                  "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "settings.py\n```\nVALUE = 2\n```\n"}}],
        usage={"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2},
    )


litellm.completion = completion
root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
os.chdir(root)
target = root / "settings.py"
target.write_text("VALUE = 1\n")
target.chmod(stat.S_IRUSR)  # read-only: the write will fail with PermissionError

io = InputOutput(pretty=False, fancy_input=False, yes=True)
coder = Coder.create(main_model=Model("gpt-4o"), io=io, fnames=[str(target)], edit_format="whole",
                     use_git=False, stream=False, map_tokens=0, suggest_shell_commands=False)
coder.run(with_message="Set VALUE to 2.")

print("--- after the run")
print("file content:", repr(target.read_text()))
print("aider_edited_files:", sorted(coder.aider_edited_files))
print("last messages in history:", [(m["role"], m["content"]) for m in coder.done_messages[-2:]])
```

3. Run `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-none python repro.py` as a non-root user (root ignores the read-only bit).

## Actual output

````text
aider 0.86.0
settings.py

```diff
@@ -1 +1 @@
-VALUE = 1
+VALUE = 2
```


Tokens: 1 sent, 1 received. Cost: $0.000013 message, $0.000013 session.
Unable to write file /tmp/tmpXXXX/settings.py after 5 attempts: [Errno 13] 
Permission denied: '/tmp/tmpXXXX/settings.py'
[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/tmp/tmpXXXX/settings.py'
--- after the run
file content: 'VALUE = 1\n'
aider_edited_files: ['settings.py']
last messages in history: [('user', 'I updated the files.'), ('assistant', 'Ok.')]
````

`main` at `5dc9490b` prints the same (only the version line and temp paths differ). The same happens for other `OSError`s raised while writing, e.g. when the target path has been replaced by a directory.

## Expected behavior

A failed write should not be recorded as a successful edit. Either the error should be reflected to the model (as the generic `except Exception` branch of `apply_updates` already does via `reflected_message`), or at least the file should not be added to the edited set and "I updated the files." should not be added to the history.

## Root cause

[`apply_updates`](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L2296-L2320) computes `edited` from the parsed edits before writing, and its `except ANY_GIT_ERROR` branch returns that set after only printing the error. `ANY_GIT_ERROR` includes `OSError` ([repo.py L26-L35](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/repo.py#L26-L35)), so a write failure from `io.write_text` takes this branch. [`send_message`](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/base_coder.py#L1585-L1594) then treats the returned set as applied edits: it updates `aider_edited_files`, auto-commits (in a repo), and moves `files_content_gpt_edits_no_repo` ("I updated the files.") into the history.

## Possible fix direction

Return an empty set (or let the write failure reach the generic branch so `reflected_message` is set) when the write itself fails, so only files that were actually written are reported as edited.

### Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.0` (PyPI) and `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c` (`0.86.3.dev0`)
Model: `gpt-4o` with `litellm.completion` scripted (no real model call)
Edit format: `whole`; no git repo
Python: `3.12.13`
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS

unique_issues.title: Arbitrary Command Execution in Aider via Auto-Loaded .aider.conf.yml Command Keys (notifications-command, editor)
unique_issues.body:
### Issue

Package : Aider-AI/aider (PyPI: aider-chat)

Tested Versions : 0.86.2 (latest PyPI release); default-branch HEAD 5dc9490 (0.86.3.dev)

---

## Affected Files

- aider/main.py (config wiring: notifications, notifications_command, editor passed from parsed args into InputOutput and Commands)
- aider/io.py (InputOutput.ring_bell)
- aider/editor.py (pipe_editor, discover_editor)
- aider/commands.py (Commands.editor / cmd_editor)

---

## Root Cause

Aider is built on configargparse, so every command-line flag is also accepted as a key in .aider.conf.yml, and that file is auto-loaded from the current working directory, the git repository root, and the home directory. When a user opens an attacker-controlled repository, the attacker's .aider.conf.yml at the repo root supplies live settings with no trust prompt. Two of these settings are strings that Aider later executes through a shell, and neither passes through the confirmation path that gates LLM-suggested shell commands.

The notifications-command value flows from args.notifications_command into InputOutput, where ring_bell runs it with subprocess.run(self.notifications_command, shell=True). The command is executed when bell_on_next_input is set and notifications is enabled. Because the attacker controls the whole config file, the same file sets notifications to true alongside notifications-command, satisfying the guard. After the victim sends one message and the model replies, llm_started sets bell_on_next_input, and the next input prompt calls ring_bell, firing the attacker command, and it fires again on every subsequent turn.

The editor value flows from args.editor into Commands and is used by pipe_editor, which builds a command string by concatenating discover_editor(editor) with the temporary file path and runs it with subprocess.call(command_str, shell=True). discover_editor returns the configured editor override verbatim, so a value such as "vim; <command>" is shell-interpreted and the appended commands run. This path is reached when the victim uses the normal /editor command (or the Ctrl-X Ctrl-E input binding) to compose a message.

In both cases the attacker-chosen string is passed to a shell with shell=True and no confirmation, so control of the repository yields command execution as the user running Aider.

---

## PoC

1. Attacker publishes a normal-looking repository whose root contains a crafted .aider.conf.yml, for example setting notifications to true with notifications-command set to a marker command (such as a file-creating command), and editor set to a value like "vim; <marker command>".
2. Victim clones the repository and runs aider inside it. The repo-root .aider.conf.yml is auto-loaded, so the attacker values become the active notifications_command and editor settings.
3. Victim sends one message and the model replies. On the next input prompt, ring_bell executes the notifications-command value through the shell with no prompt, and it repeats on later turns.
4. Victim runs the /editor command to compose a message. pipe_editor executes the editor value through the shell with no prompt.

In the researcher's end-to-end run on aider 0.86.2 using a local mock LLM with no API key and no external network, a single interactive session triggered both sinks: sending a message created the notifications canary file and running /editor created the editor canary file, each with no confirmation prompt.

---

## Impact

An attacker who controls a repository that a victim opens with Aider can execute arbitrary commands as the victim, with no approval prompt, through either of two auto-loaded configuration keys. The notifications-command path fires automatically after the first model response and on every later turn, so no special user action beyond normal use is required; the editor path fires when the victim uses the ordinary /editor feature. Execution runs with the victim's privileges and can read or modify local files, steal credentials, or establish further access. This is the same class of exposure as the previously assigned test-cmd and lint-cmd keys, reached through two distinct, uncovered sinks.

---

## Suggested Remediation

Treat a repository-root .aider.conf.yml as untrusted and distinguish repository-local configuration from user and home configuration. Require a one-time user trust prompt before honoring command-bearing keys loaded from a repository-local config (test-cmd, lint-cmd, notifications-command, editor), comparable to editor and IDE workspace-trust models. For notifications-command and editor specifically, confirm before the first execution and prefer argument-list execution over shell=True.

---
Reporter : Seoyoung Lee. Reported to VulnCheck; published here as a public reference for CVE assignment, as the project has no dedicated security reporting channel.

### Version and model info

Aider 0.86.2 (PyPI). Model: N/A (mock LLM) — config-sourced, model-independent.

unique_issues.title: Batch mode for bulk edits via provider batch APIs (preview-then-submit plan workflow)
unique_issues.body:
Aider executes every LLM request at realtime rates, which makes bulk, independent single-turn tasks (repo-wide codemods, doc translation, per-file extraction) expensive and serial.

Proposal (design discussion only, per CONTRIBUTING): an opt-in batch subsystem modeled on provider Batch APIs, scoped in v1 to one OpenAI-compatible executor:

- `aider batch check` — validate provider/model selection without billing.
- `aider batch run <plan.json> --dry-run` — preview item count, model, target directories and a token estimate; prints a snapshot hash; uploads nothing.
- `aider batch run <plan.json> --expect <snapshot>` — submit only if plan, sources and settings still match the preview.
- `aider batch collect <task-id> [--wait]` — reconcile results; report each item delivered / held (source changed or target differs) / failed; never auto-retry billed items.
- Task records under a cache dir with owner-only permissions; targets restricted to in-project, non-hidden paths since results land hours after approval.

Peer precedent: qwen-code's user docs describe exactly this workflow at ~50% of realtime price, including the caveat that batch only wins when little of each request shares a cached prefix (it loses beyond ~0.625 cache-hit rate), so normal chat turns must never be routed through it.

Open questions for maintainers: which provider(s) in v1, plan-file schema, whether interactive sessions should auto-collect finished tasks, and whether this belongs in core or behind an extension seam. No implementation is attached; this is the pre-PR discussion CONTRIBUTING requests for large changes.

## Research evidence (static; tests pending)

- https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/7c4c7fa652c3910bbda8e787af66274248fcd026/docs/users/features/batch.md
  > The DashScope Batch API runs requests asynchronously at half the realtime
price, with a completion window of at least 24 hours.
- https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/7c4c7fa652c3910bbda8e787af66274248fcd026/docs/users/features/batch.md
  > qwen batch check                         # verify setup; nothing is billed
- https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/7c4c7fa652c3910bbda8e787af66274248fcd026/docs/users/features/batch.md
  > Failed items are never retried
automatically, since a retry bills again.
- https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/shell.py
  > Only suggest at most a few shell commands at a time, not more than 1-3, one per line.
- https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c/aider/coders/ask_coder.py
  > """Ask questions about code without making any changes."""

### Users

Cost-sensitive aider users running large numbers of independent single-turn requests (bulk file updates, documentation translation, per-file data extraction, mass test generation) and CI/automation pipelines embedding aider for unattended bulk jobs.

### Expected Effect

Qualifying bulk workloads run at roughly half the realtime list price without holding an interactive session; a mandatory dry-run preview plus snapshot hash prevents surprise billing and stale-plan submission; per-item delivered/held/failed reporting makes collection safe to re-run.

### Scope

New aider/batch.py (or aider/batch/ package) plus CLI wiring in aider/args.py and aider/main.py; task record store under a cache dir; docs page under aider/website/docs; tests under tests/basic/test_batch.py. v1 limited to a single OpenAI-compatible chat-completions batch executor; no changes to existing coder edit paths.

### Validation

Commands: pytest tests/basic/test_batch.py; aider batch check (exits 0 with valid config, non-zero with actionable error otherwise); aider batch run plan.json --dry-run (prints item count, model, target dirs, token estimate and snapshot hash; performs zero uploads/billing); aider batch run plan.json --expect <snapshot> (refuses on any plan/source/settings drift); aider batch collect <task-id> (idempotent: delivered items never rewritten; changed-source and hidden-path targets marked held; failed items never auto-retried). Affected files: aider/batch.py, aider/args.py, aider/main.py, tests/basic/test_batch.py, aider/website/docs/batch.md.

### Risks

Provider batch APIs differ across vendors so v1 must be pinned to one executor; results arriving hours after approval require source-staleness and hidden-path guards; careless defaults could route interactive turns through batch and regress latency; billing footguns require the preview-plus-snapshot gate; peer implementation details are inferred from documentation only.

### Effort

Large: new command surface, plan schema with snapshot hashing, task record store with owner-only permissions, submission/polling/reconciliation, staleness and hidden-path guards, docs and tests. Multiple days; CONTRIBUTING requires issue discussion before a PR of this size.

### Acceptance

Uncertain-to-moderate. Aider regularly merges scoped provider and CLI features per its release history, and CONTRIBUTING explicitly welcomes feature-request issues; but this is a significant new subsystem requiring maintainer design approval and a signed CLA before any PR. Framing the issue as a v1-scoped proposal (single OpenAI-compatible executor, opt-in only) matches the documented pricing trade-off and improves odds.

### Comparison

qwen-code's official docs document this end-to-end: '/batch-api' plan authoring, 'qwen batch run --dry-run' previewing '42 item(s), window 24h — nothing uploaded, nothing billed', submission gated on '--expect <snapshot>', background 'collect --wait', records in '~/.qwen/batch/tasks/<task-id>/' with owner-only permissions, targets restricted to in-project non-hidden paths, and the explicit caveat that batch loses once shared-prefix cache hit rates exceed ~0.625. Aider's supplied paths show no batch surface; the nearest mechanism is serial scripted runs at full price. Peer implementation code was not supplied, so this comparison rests on official docs only.

Maintainer direction requested before implementation.

AI-assisted contribution.

<!-- oss-contributor:8705199c29c365625225e2c8 -->
