unique_issues.body: ### Before submitting your bug report - [x] I've tried finding an answer on the [Continue docs site](https://docs.continue.dev/) - [ ] I'm not able to find an [open issue](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue) that reports the same bug - [x] I've seen the [troubleshooting guide](https://docs.continue.dev/troubleshooting) on the Continue Docs ### Relevant environment info ```Markdown - OS: Windows 10 LTSC 21H2 - Continue version: 2.0.0 - IDE version: VSCodium 1.135.06.55 - Model: qwen3.8:27b - config: name: Local Max VRAM Config version: 1.0.0 schema: v1 models: - name: Qwen 3.8 27b (256K) provider: ollama model: qwen3.8:27b contextLength: 64000 defaultCompletionOptions: temperature: 0 contextLength: 32000 maxTokens: 16000 capabilities: - tool_use roles: [chat, edit, apply, summarize] timeout: 120000 - name: Qwen 2.5 coder 32b (32K) provider: ollama model: qwen2.5-coder:32b contextLength: 32000 defaultCompletionOptions: temperature: 0 contextLength: 32000 maxTokens: 16000 roles: [chat, edit, apply, autocomplete] timeout: 120000 - name: Apply model provider: ollama model: qwen2.5-coder:1.5b contextLength: 32000 defaultCompletionOptions: temperature: 0 contextLength: 32000 maxTokens: 16000 roles: [apply, autocomplete] timeout: 120000 - name: Nomic Embed provider: ollama model: nomic-embed-text:latest roles: - embed mcpServers: - name: filesystem command: node args: - "E:\\GPT\\Ollama\\mcp-tee.js" - "-y" - "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem" - "E:\\www\\letbox\\docker\\dms\\dms-gui" VScodium about: Version: 1.135.06055 Commit: 1a46a584725d5dd330e0bcd7f5510f24990efcf2 Date: 2026-08-25T14:26:52Z Electron: 42.8.1 ElectronBuildId: undefined Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 Node.js: 24.18.1 V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0 @github/copilot: Unknown @github/copilot-sdk: Unknown OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19044 ``` ### Description Continue intermittently fails to pass an array to the tools requiring an array. I got the bug with **read_file** and therefore, resorted to use nodeJS mcp filesystem tool with same problems. * project: classic ReactJS I am trying to fix bugs for * prompt: `Fix the blatant bugs in @DataTable.jsx and offer code change with comments above the changes, directly into the file. Add more context by reading maximum 3 files that either use this component or are critical for the component to work.` * result: * Errors seen from the IDE: ``` filesystem_read_multiple_files failed with the message: [{"type":"text","text":"MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool read_multiple_files: Invalid input: expected array, received string at paths"}] filesystem_edit_file failed with the message: [{"type":"text","text":"MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool edit_file: Invalid input: expected array, received string at edits\nInvalid input: expected boolean, received string at dryRun"}] ``` ### To reproduce I have concentrated my research on **filesystem_read_multiple_files** because it's easy to reproduce. The first call works, it reads the files, the second call fails, always. In both cases, the TRACE log from ollama always reports the same command: ``` time=2026-10-05T16:30:29.366-07:00 level=TRACE source=qwen3coder.go:117 msg="qwen events parsed" events="[{raw:\n\n\n[\"common.mjs\",\"frontend/src/frontend.mjs\", \"frontend/src/components/AlertMessage.jsx\"]\n\n\n}]" state=0 acc="" time=2026-10-05T16:30:42.541-07:00 level=TRACE source=qwen3coder.go:117 msg="qwen events parsed" events="[{raw:\n\n\n[\"frontend/src/pages/Logins.jsx\",\"frontend/src/pages/Accounts.jsx\",\"frontend/src/components/Translate.jsx\"]\n\n\n}]" state=0 acc="" ``` VSCodium dev console logs nothing at all, so I resorted to a trick to log what Continue sends to the filesystem server: Put a small wrapper between Continue and the server that copies everything Continue sends it into a file. ```js const { spawn } = require('child_process'); const fs = require('fs'); const log = fs.createWriteStream('"E:\\GPT\\Ollama\\mcp-tee.log', { flags: 'a' }); const child = spawn('npx.cmd', process.argv.slice(2), { stdio: ['pipe', 'inherit', 'inherit'], shell: true }); process.stdin.on('data', d => { log.write(d); child.stdin.write(d); }); process.stdin.on('end', () => child.stdin.end()); child.on('exit', c => process.exit(c)); ``` The config.yaml reflects the use of that wrapper. The wrapper log is telling! ```json {"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"continue-client","version":"1.0.0"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0} {"method":"notifications/initialized","jsonrpc":"2.0"} {"method":"tools/list","params":{},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1} {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_multiple_files","arguments":{"paths":["common.mjs","frontend/src/frontend.mjs","frontend/src/components/AlertMessage.jsx"]}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2} {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_multiple_files","arguments":{"paths":"[\"frontend/src/pages/Accounts.jsx\",\"frontend/src/components/Translate.jsx\"]"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3} {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_text_file","arguments":{"path":"frontend/src/pages/Accounts.jsx"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4} {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_text_file","arguments":{"path":"frontend/src/components/Translate.jsx"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5} ``` That capture is the strongest evidence: the same tool, the same schema, and the same kind of valid model output, yet call 3 arrives at the server as a quoted string while call 2 arrives as a real array. So the string is created before Continue writes to the MCP server. The wrapper only sees the end of the chain, so it can't say whether Ollama returned a string or Continue stringified it. The two suspects are: - Ollama's qwen3coder parser - Continue after it receives the call. It's really sad because everything else almost work. ### Log output ```Shell filesystem_read_multiple_files failed with the message: [{"type":"text","text":"MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool read_multiple_files: Invalid input: expected array, received string at paths"}] filesystem_edit_file failed with the message: [{"type":"text","text":"MCP error -32602: Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool edit_file: Invalid input: expected array, received string at edits\nInvalid input: expected boolean, received string at dryRun"}] ```

unique_issues.title: create_new_file writes a JSON file on one line when the model sends its contents as a JSON value
unique_issues.body:
### Relevant environment info

- OS: macOS
- Continue version: 2.0.0 (also checked on main at 5522c6f)
- IDE version: VS Code 1.141.0
- Model: Qwen3.6-Coder 35B, served locally through an OpenAI-compatible API (provider `openai`)

### Description

When a model sends the `contents` of a new `.json` file as a JSON value instead of a string, `create_new_file` writes the file on a single line, for example:

```json
{"name":"app","version":"1.0.0","scripts":{"build":"tsc"},"devDependencies":{"typescript":"^5.6.0"}}
```

A `package.json` or `tsconfig.json` written like this is valid, but nobody would write it that way, and every later edit produces a large diff.

Cause: `createNewFileImpl` reads the contents with `getStringArg`, which turns an object back into text with `JSON.stringify(value)`. That compact form is right for other string arguments (and is what the existing tests expect), but for the contents of a file, indented JSON (`JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)`) is what the model meant.

### To reproduce

Call `createNewFileImpl({ filepath: "app/package.json", contents: { name: "app", private: true } }, extras)`: the file is written as `{"name":"app","private":true}`.

### Log output

_No response_

unique_issues.title: Windows absolute paths are parsed as remote package slugs
unique_issues.body:
Windows absolute paths are classified as remote package slugs by `decodePackageIdentifier`.

On main (`5522c6f`), `C:\project\rule.yaml`, `C:/project/rule.yaml`, and `\\server\share\rule.yaml` all return `uriType: "slug"`. The forward-slash drive path even becomes owner `C:`, package `project`, version `rule.yaml`. Relative paths and POSIX absolute paths correctly return `uriType: "file"`.

This parser is used by YAML `uses` references and the CLI model/MCP/rule inputs, so these Windows paths are sent down the package-resolution path instead of local file loading. I reproduced the parser outputs directly from the current source.

I plan to recognize drive-absolute and UNC paths, preserving the supplied path and leaving package slugs unchanged, with cross-platform regression tests.

unique_issues.title: Standard Unreal Engine C++ Private directories incorrectly blocked by security filter
unique_issues.body:
### Before submitting your bug report

- [x] I've tried finding an answer on the [Continue docs site](https://docs.continue.dev/)
- [x] I'm not able to find an [open issue](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue) that reports the same bug
- [x] I've seen the [troubleshooting guide](https://docs.continue.dev/troubleshooting) on the Continue Docs

### Relevant environment info

```Markdown
- OS: Windows
- Continue version: 2.0.0
- IDE version: VS Code 1.143.1
- Model: Qwen3 14B
- Mode: Agent
- Game engine: Unreal Engine 5.8
- Project type: C++
```

### Description

## Description

Continue's built-in security filter appears to incorrectly block access to C++ source files located inside Unreal Engine's standard `Private` directory.

Unreal Engine 5.8 officially recommends using Public and Private directories for organizing C++ modules. The `Private` directory contains ordinary implementation files (`.cpp`), not necessarily sensitive information.

Continue's Agent Mode rejects file operations within this directory and reports them as security concerns.

This interferes with normal Unreal Engine C++ development workflows.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or open any Unreal Engine C++ project in Visual Studio Code.
2. Use the standard Unreal Engine module structure:

   ```
   ExampleProject/
   └── Source/
       └── ExampleModule/
           ├── Public/
           │   └── ExampleActor.h
           └── Private/
               └── ExampleActor.cpp
   ```

3. Open Continue in Agent Mode.
4. Ask the agent to create or modify `Source/ExampleModule/Private/ExampleActor.cpp`.
5. Observe the security error.

Creating the corresponding header file in the `Public` directory succeeds.

## Actual Behavior

The `create_new_file` tool fails with an error similar to:

```
create_new_file failed with the message:

Reading or Editing
c%3A/Users/<username>/Documents/ExampleProject/
Source/ExampleModule/Private/ExampleActor.cpp
is not allowed because it is a security concern.

Do not attempt to read or edit this file in any way.
```

The agent cannot proceed with normal C++ implementation work inside the `Private` directory.

## Expected Behavior

Continue should allow reading, creating and modifying C++ files inside standard Unreal Engine `Source/<ModuleName>/Private/` directories when the user has authorized access to the workspace.

The directory name `Private` should not automatically cause normal C++ source files to be classified as sensitive.

## Suspected Root Cause

Continue's security ignore configuration includes directory names such as:

```typescript
export const DEFAULT_SECURITY_IGNORE_DIRS = [
  // ...
  "private/",
  ".private/",
  // ...
];
```

The security checks may be matching Unreal Engine's `Private` directory without considering its purpose as a standard source-code directory.

Relevant source file:

https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/main/core/indexing/ignore.ts

## Suggested Solutions

1. Provide a workspace-scoped allowlist for trusted source-code directories.
2. Allow users to explicitly approve access to standard Unreal Engine `Source/<ModuleName>/Private/` directories.
3. Improve security filtering to distinguish sensitive private-data directories from ordinary C++ implementation directories.

Preferably, these exceptions should not require users to disable security protections globally.

## Additional Information

The agent successfully created a C++ header file inside the `Public` directory but failed when attempting to create the corresponding `.cpp` implementation file inside `Private`.

This suggests the issue is related to Continue's file access security checks rather than the underlying language model or filesystem permissions.

Thank you for looking into this!

unique_issues.title: Feature request: Support `tools: ['*']` wildcard in custom agents
unique_issues.body:
## Problem

Custom agents (`.agent.md` files) require explicit tool lists in the YAML frontmatter. There is no wildcard to include "all available tools."

This creates maintenance burden and user confusion:

1. **New tools require manual updates**: When VS Code adds new built-in tools, custom agents don't automatically get access. Maintainers must update every `.agent.md` file.

2. **Tool lists are long and duplicative**: To match the default Agent's capabilities, a custom agent needs 30+ tool entries. This clutters the frontmatter and obscures the agent's actual purpose.

3. **Users expect parity**: When switching from the default Agent to a custom agent, users expect the same tools to be available. Discovering that `multi_replace_string_in_file` is missing (for example) is frustrating.

## Proposed Solution

Allow a wildcard in the `tools:` array that includes all available tools:

```yaml
---
name: My Agent
tools: ['*']  # All built-in tools + all MCP tools
---
```

Or more granularly:

```yaml
---
name: My Agent
tools: ['builtin/*', 'my-mcp-server/*']  # All built-in + specific MCP
---
```

## Current Workaround

Manually enumerate all known tools:

```yaml
tools:
  - 'my-mcp/*'
  - 'read_file'
  - 'replace_string_in_file'
  - 'multi_replace_string_in_file'
  - 'create_file'
  - 'create_directory'
  - 'list_dir'
  - 'file_search'
  - 'grep_search'
  - 'semantic_search'
  - 'list_code_usages'
  - 'get_errors'
  - 'run_in_terminal'
  - 'get_terminal_output'
  - 'terminal_last_command'
  - 'terminal_selection'
  - 'run_task'
  - 'create_and_run_task'
  - 'get_task_output'
  - 'get_changed_files'
  - 'search'
  - 'fetch'
  - 'fetch_webpage'
  - 'edit_notebook_file'
  - 'run_notebook_cell'
  - 'read_notebook_cell_output'
  - 'copilot_getNotebookSummary'
  - 'create_new_jupyter_notebook'
  - 'test_failure'
  - 'manage_todo_list'
  # ... and any others I've missed
```

This is fragile and will break as VS Code evolves.

## Use Case

I'm building a custom agent with a specific persona and instructions. The agent should have access to all the same tools as the default Agent, plus my MCP server tools. The persona and instructions are what differentiate my agent, not a restricted tool set.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.96.x
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension: latest
- OS: Linux

unique_issues.title: Configure Tools UI writes incorrect tool names with prefix notation, corrupting custom agent files
unique_issues.body:
## Environment
- VS Code Version: 1.108.2
- Copilot Chat Extension: 0.36.2
- OS: macOS

## Bug Description
The "Configure Tools" UI (wrench/screwdriver icon in chat) writes **incorrect tool names** back to `.agent.md` files, using an internal prefix notation that doesn't work.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create custom agent `.github/agents/MyAgent.agent.md` with correct tools:
   ```yaml
   tools: ['runInTerminal', 'getTerminalOutput', 'readFile', 'createFile', 'editFiles']
   ```
2. Select the custom agent in chat
3. Click the "Configure Tools" icon (wrench/screwdriver)
4. See 5 tools displayed correctly
5. Click OK (or just wait ~30 minutes)
6. **Result:** File is overwritten with WRONG format:
   ```yaml
   tools: ['execute/runInTerminal', 'execute/getTerminalOutput', 'read/readFile', 'edit/createFile', 'edit/editFiles']
   ```

## The Problem
The prefix notation (`execute/`, `read/`, `edit/`, `search/`) is **not recognized** by the agent system. After this corruption:
- Agent reports all tools as "disabled"
- Agent suggests user enable tools in settings (which doesn't help)
- Only fix is to manually correct the file

## Additional Issue
This corruption also happens **automatically** without clicking the Configure Tools button - approximately every 30-33 minutes during active use. Suspected periodic state sync that uses the wrong format.

## Workaround
Set agent files to read-only:
```bash
chmod 444 .github/agents/*.agent.md
```
This causes an error when VS Code tries to overwrite, but preserves the correct config.

## Expected Behavior
- Configure Tools UI should write the **correct** tool names without prefixes

unique_issues.title: ask_questions tool always returns skipped:true regardless of user input
unique_issues.body:
## Description

The `ask_questions` tool consistently returns `{"skipped":true}` in the function results WITHOUT presenting any UI to the user. The quick pick dialog never appears, and the tool immediately returns as if the user skipped the question.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the `ask_questions` tool with any question and options
2. Observe that no quick pick dialog appears
3. The function result immediately returns with `{"skipped":true}`

## Expected Behavior

1. A quick pick dialog should appear with the question and options
2. User can select an option or provide free text input
3. The function result should contain either:
   - `{"selected": ["Option Label"]}` when an option is selected
   - `{"freeText": "user input"}` when free text is provided
   - `{"skipped": true}` only when the user explicitly dismisses/skips the question (ESC key)

## Actual Behavior

No UI is presented to the user. The tool immediately returns:
```json
{"answers":{"Header":{"selected":[],"freeText":null,"skipped":true}}}
```

The user has no opportunity to interact with the question.

## Example Tool Call

```json
{
  "questions": [{
    "allowFreeformInput": false,
    "header": "Test",
    "options": [
      {"label": "Option A"},
      {"label": "Option B"}
    ],
    "question": "Can you select one of these options?"
  }]
}
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- VS Code: Insiders
- GitHub Copilot: Latest
- Date: February 1, 2026

## Impact

This makes the `ask_questions` tool completely non-functional, preventing agents from gathering user preferences or clarifying intent through structured questions. The tool documentation suggests it should present interactive UI, but no UI appears at all.

• **Logs:** See below

---

## Summary

When using Claude models (e.g., Claude Opus 4.5) in Copilot Agent Mode, MCP tools from workspace-configured servers are shown as "disabled by user" and cannot be invoked, despite the MCP server running correctly and responding to HTTP requests.

The VS Code Window log shows:
```
chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: claude-code
[UriError]: Scheme contains illegal characters.
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an MCP server in `.vscode/mcp.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "servers": {
       "my-server": {
         "url": "http://127.0.0.1:7654/mcp"
       }
     }
   }
   ```
2. Start the MCP server (verified working via `curl` - returns valid JSON-RPC responses to `tools/list` and `tools/call`)
3. Open Copilot Chat in Agent Mode
4. Select Claude Opus 4.5 (or other Claude model) as the model
5. Attempt to use MCP tools
6. Observe: Tools show as "disabled by user" and cannot be called

## Expected Behavior

MCP tools should be available and callable when using Claude models, the same as with GPT models.

## Actual Behavior

- MCP tools appear in the tool list but are marked as disabled
- Attempting to call them returns "Tool is currently disabled by the user"
- The error `chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: claude-code` appears in Window logs
- The MCP server itself is functioning correctly (verified via direct HTTP calls)

## Additional Info

  ```bash
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "Accept: application/json" \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' 
  # Returns valid tool list
  ```

unique_issues.title: Allow expanded display of auto-approved terminal commands

## Feature Request

**Problem:** When terminal commands are added to `github.copilot.chat.terminalCommands.autoApproval`, they are displayed in a minimized/compact text block. There is no way to auto-approve commands while still seeing them displayed prominently in the chat.

**Current behavior:** Command visibility is coupled to approval status — auto-approved commands are always minimized, while commands requiring approval are shown prominently.

unique_issues.title: Parser line length limit causes false 'Session file is corrupted' error
unique_issues.body: ## TL;DR Session parser fails on lines >15KB, reports misleading "Session file is corrupted" error instead of "line too long". Error occurs on line immediately after longest line, both containing duplicated ~14KB skill content. Makes chat completely unusable until window reload. ## Environment - **VS Code Versions:** Both latest Stable AND latest Insiders - **Architecture:** arm64 (Apple Silicon) - **OS:** macOS - **Extensions:** GitHub Copilot with background agents (actually a Copilot CLI agent running in a separate terminal, which shows up as a background agent in vscode) ## Impact - **Severity:** High - Chat becomes completely unusable until window reload - After selecting the corrupted session, ALL subsequent chat attempts fail - No data loss, but significant disruption - Affects both stable and Insiders ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Start a background Copilot agent session with custom agent 2. Agent performs long workflow loading large skills (25+ turns) 3. Session completes successfully, writes events to `~/.copilot/session-state/{sessionId}/events.jsonl` 4. Try to open the session from background agents list in VS Code 5. Error: "Failed to open chat session: Session file is corrupted (line...)" 6. All subsequent chat attempts fail until window reload ## Root Cause **Critical Finding:** Error reports line 15, immediately after longest line (14). ### The Smoking Gun - **Line 14:** `tool.execution_complete` - 15,416 chars (skill result with ~14KB skill content) - **Line 15:** `skill.invoked` - 15,155 chars (same skill content duplicated) Both lines contain **full skill file content** (~14KB) from loaded skill: ```json Line 14: { "type": "tool.execution_complete", "data": { "result": { "detailedContent": "Skill loaded successfully ✅\n\n---\n[14KB SKILL.md content]..." } } } Line 15: { "type": "skill.invoked", "data": { "content": "[14KB SKILL.md content]..." } } ``` ### Why This Breaks 1. Parser has **line length limit** (~8-16KB typical for JSONL parsers) 2. Parser reads line 14 (15KB) - pushes limit but succeeds 3. Parser reads line 15 (another 15KB) - **fails**, reports error on line 15 4. Error says "corrupted" instead of "line length limit exceeded" ### Validation ```bash # All 138 lines pass JSON validation while IFS= read -r line; do echo "$line" | jq empty || exit 1 done < events.jsonl # Result: ALL lines are valid JSON ``` ## Session Details - **File size:** 192KB - **Lines:** 138 - **Turns:** 26 completed turns - **Largest line:** 15,415 chars (line 14) - **Format:** Valid JSONL - each line is valid JSON - Session ended cleanly with proper turn pairs ## Suggested Fixes ### Immediate (Critical) 1. **Fix error message:** "Session file is corrupted" → "Line length limit exceeded" or "Parser buffer overflow" 2. **Increase line length limit:** 15KB lines are reasonable for JSON with embedded content 3. **Prevent cascade failure:** One failed session shouldn't break ALL chat functionality 4. **Graceful degradation:** Show partial session or summary view instead of total failure ### Architecture Issues 1. **Eliminate duplication:** Don't store full skill content in BOTH `tool.execution_complete` AND `skill.invoked` events 2. **Use references:** Store large content once with ID, reference by ID in events 3. **Consider multi-line JSON:** Proper JSON formatting vs cramming on one line 4. **Compression:** Gzip large content fields before storing ### Long-term 1. Streaming/pagination for large sessions 2. Add session file size limits with warnings at write time 3. Separate metadata from full event log ## Workaround Delete the session directory: ```bash rm -rf ~/.copilot/session-state/{sessionId} ``` Then reload VS Code window. ## Context The Copilot CLI session was completely successful - it created work items, synced repos, created PRs, passed validation. The "corruption" error is a **false positive** caused by parser limits that makes all chat unusable, not just that session. In fact, the session is still active. **Key insight:** Error pointing to line 15 (right after longest line 14) is classic parser buffer overflow pattern, NOT corruption. ## Related Questions - Where is session file format/schema documented? - Are there documented limits for line lengths? - Why does one failed session break ALL chat functionality? Session ID available for debugging: `5064615a-1135-472b-ac5c-76e379714b86`

unique_issues.title: Copilot CLI bootstrapper infinite-loops when both VS Code and VS Code Insiders are installed
unique_issues.body:
## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **VS Code Insiders:** Latest (updates twice daily)
- **VS Code (stable):** Also installed
- **Copilot CLI:** Installed via winget (`GitHub.Copilot v0.0.405`)
- **PowerShell:** 7.x

## Bug

Running `copilot` in any VS Code terminal hangs indefinitely. The command never returns.

## Root Cause

The bootstrapper script `copilot.ps1` (bundled with the `github.copilot-chat` extension) has a bug in `Find-RealCopilot` when **two VS Code installations** (Stable + Insiders) are both present. Each installation injects its own `copilotCli` directory into the terminal's `PATH`:

```
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Code - Insiders\User\globalStorage\github.copilot-chat\copilotCli
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\globalStorage\github.copilot-chat\copilotCli
```

Each directory contains `copilot.ps1` and `copilot.bat`.

### The infinite loop

1. User types `copilot` → PowerShell finds Insiders' `copilot.ps1`
2. `Find-RealCopilot` detects that `Get-Command copilot` points to itself
3. It strips **only its own directory** from `$env:PATH`
4. Calls `Get-Command copilot` again → now finds Stable's `copilot.bat`
5. Returns `copilot.bat` as the "real" copilot binary ❌
6. `Test-AndLaunchCopilot` executes Stable's `copilot.bat`
7. `copilot.bat` launches Stable's `copilot.ps1`
8. Stable's `Find-RealCopilot` strips **its own directory** from PATH
9. Calls `Get-Command copilot` → finds Insiders' `copilot.bat`
10. Returns it as the "real" binary → executes it → **GOTO 2**

This creates an infinite recursion that hangs the terminal.

### Relevant code in `Find-RealCopilot`

```powershell
# The copilot in PATH is this script, find the real one by temporarily removing 
# this script's directory from PATH
$ScriptDir = Split-Path $CurrentScript -Parent
$OldPath = $env:PATH
$env:PATH = ($env:PATH -split $PathDelimiter | Where-Object { $_ -ne $ScriptDir }) -join $PathDelimiter
$RealCopilot = (Get-Command copilot -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source  # finds the OTHER VS Code's copilot.bat
$env:PATH = $OldPath
```

The problem: it only strips `$ScriptDir` (its own directory), not **all** `copilotCli` directories.

## Suggested Fix

Strip all `copilotCli` directories from PATH when searching for the real binary, not just the current script's directory. For example:

```powershell
# Instead of:
$env:PATH = ($env:PATH -split $PathDelimiter | Where-Object { $_ -ne $ScriptDir }) -join $PathDelimiter

# Do:
$env:PATH = ($env:PATH -split $PathDelimiter | Where-Object { 
    $_ -ne $ScriptDir -and $_ -notlike '*copilotCli*'
}) -join $PathDelimiter
```

Or alternatively, search specifically for `copilot.exe` rather than just `copilot` (which matches `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd` etc. via `PATHEXT`):

```powershell
$RealCopilot = (Get-Command copilot.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source
```

## Reproduction Steps

1. Install both VS Code Stable and VS Code Insiders
2. Install Copilot CLI via winget (`winget install GitHub.Copilot`)
3. Open VS Code Insiders
4. Open any terminal (PowerShell)
5. Type `copilot`
6. Observe: command hangs, never returns

## Workaround

Define a PowerShell function in `profile.ps1` (AllHosts) that directly invokes the winget-installed binary, bypassing PATH resolution entirely:

```powershell
function copilot {
    & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\GitHub.Copilot_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe\copilot.exe" @args
}
```

This works but is fragile — the winget package path could change between versions.

- **VS Code Stable:** latest
- **VS Code Insiders:** latest
- **Copilot extension:** latest on both

unique_issues.title: Feature Request: Add settings option to control ask_questions auto-approve behavior
unique_issues.body:
## Description

When `chat.agent.autoApprove` is set to `true`, the `ask_questions` tool is also auto-approved, causing it to always return `{"skipped": true}` without presenting any UI to the user. There is **no setting in VS Code** to independently control the auto-approve behavior of `ask_questions`.

## Current Behavior

- `chat.agent.autoApprove: true` auto-approves **all** tools, including `ask_questions`
- Terminal commands have granular control via `chat.agent.autoApprove.terminal.allowList` / `chat.agent.autoApprove.terminal.commands`
- But there is **no equivalent setting** for `ask_questions`: no `chat.agent.autoApprove.askQuestions` or similar option exists
- This means users who want auto-approve for file edits, searches, terminal commands etc. are forced to also auto-approve `ask_questions`, which defeats the purpose of the tool

## Expected Behavior

A dedicated setting should exist to control `ask_questions` independently, for example:

```jsonc
// Option A: Simple boolean
"chat.agent.autoApprove.askQuestions": false  // default: false

// Option B: Per-tool granularity (more general solution)
"chat.agent.autoApprove.tools": {
  "ask_questions": false,
  "read_file": true,
  "replace_string_in_file": true,
  // ...
}
```

This way, users can keep `chat.agent.autoApprove: true` for productivity while ensuring `ask_questions` always presents its UI for user interaction.

## Use Case

When using agent mode / Plan Agent, the model calls `ask_questions` to clarify requirements or confirm decisions before proceeding. With global auto-approve on, this confirmation step is silently skipped, causing the agent to proceed without user input — which defeats the purpose of Plan mode's interactive planning phase.

## Relationship to #14105

Issue #14105 reports that `ask_questions` always returns `skipped:true`. The root cause in many cases is likely `chat.agent.autoApprove: true` silently skipping the UI. Even if #14105 is fixed as a bug, a **settings-level control** for `ask_questions` auto-approve is still needed as a feature.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- VS Code: Stable (latest)
- GitHub Copilot: Latest

unique_issues.title: Terminal tool drops commands after heredoc terminator
unique_issues.body:
## Type
Bug

## Description
In Copilot terminal tool execution, inline heredocs are parsed inconsistently. A standalone heredoc works, but when a second command is appended after the heredoc terminator, the trailing command is dropped (or the shell can end up in a continued prompt state).

This matches repeated behavior we saw in session with messages like: "The terminal mangled the inline heredoc unexpectedly".

## Repro (minimal)
Run this through Copilot terminal execution:

```bash
python - <<'PY'
print('first')
PY
echo 'second'
```

## Expected
Both lines execute and output is:

```text
first
second
```

## Actual
Only heredoc payload executes:

```text
first
```

## Control case (works)
```bash
python -c "print('first')"; echo 'second'
```
Outputs:
```text
first
second
```

## Environment
- OS: macOS 26.1 (25B78)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Context: VS Code Copilot Chat terminal tool execution

## Notes
- Standalone heredoc (no trailing command) works.
- Adding commands after heredoc terminator appears to trigger truncation/parsing loss in command dispatch layer.
- We also observed occasional continued prompt state (`>`), suggesting delimiter handling can desync the terminal parser.

unique_issues.title: Delete key removes entire chat message without confirmation when message content is focused
unique_issues.body:
I can see how much thought has gone into making the Copilot Chat experience feel keyboard-driven and efficient — that clearly comes from real care for power users. And it works well in most cases.

Here's where it gets painful, though:

When you click anywhere inside a chat message — on text, on a code block, or even on an empty area within the message — that message becomes "selected" (indicated by a subtle blue border). At that point, pressing the **Delete** key instantly removes the entire message and its AI response, with no confirmation and no undo.

## Why this is a problem

This is extremely easy to trigger accidentally. During a coding session, you might click on a previous message to re-read it or copy something from it, then press Delete intending to act on a text field or terminal — only to watch an entire conversation turn vanish. The blue selection border is subtle enough that you may not even realize the message is in a "deletable" state.

This has happened to me multiple times during long sessions. It's especially disruptive because long, context-rich AI responses can't be regenerated identically.

## A broader question

It's not clear to me why individual messages need to be deletable in the first place. Wouldn't it be sufficient to keep entire chats deletable? If there is a strong reason for per-message deletion, the suggestions below would be movements in the right direction.

## What would help

- A confirmation prompt before deleting a selected message (even a simple "Delete this message?" would prevent accidental loss)
- Alternatively, require a modifier key (e.g., Ctrl+Delete) or use a right-click context menu instead of a bare Delete keypress
- An undo mechanism (Ctrl+Z to restore the deleted message) would also go a long way

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a multi-message Copilot Chat conversation
2. Click on any text, code block, or empty area within a previous message (a blue border appears around the message)
3. Press the Delete key
4. The entire message and its response are immediately and permanently removed

**Expected behavior:** Pressing Delete while a chat message is focused should either require confirmation, use a modifier key combination, or provide an undo option — not silently destroy content.

**Environment:** VS Code with GitHub Copilot Chat extension, tested with Claude Opus 4.6 model.

Thank you for building something worth caring about — that's exactly why this friction stands out.

unique_issues.title: Feature Request: Add tool_timeout_sec configuration for MCP servers in mcp.json
unique_issues.body:
## Problem Statement

When using MCP servers with VS Code Copilot Agent Mode, there is no way to configure a timeout for tool execution. If an MCP tool takes longer than expected (due to network issues, slow operations, or bugs), the Copilot agent waits indefinitely with no way to abort or timeout the operation.

This is particularly problematic for:
- **Parallel execution patterns** where child agents call tools that may hang
- **Long-running operations** that should fail fast if they exceed a threshold
- **Debugging scenarios** where developers need to test timeout handling

## Current Behavior

The `mcp.json` configuration only supports:
```json
{
  "servers": {
    "MyServer": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "dotnet",
      "args": ["run", "--project", "path/to/server.csproj"],
      "env": {}
    }
  }
}
```

There is no timeout configuration available.

## Proposed Solution

Add `tool_timeout_sec` (or similar) configuration option per MCP server:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "MyServer": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "dotnet",
      "args": ["run", "--project", "path/to/server.csproj"],
      "tool_timeout_sec": 30,
      "startup_timeout_sec": 10
    }
  }
}
```

### Configuration Options

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `tool_timeout_sec` | Maximum time to wait for a tool call to complete | 60 |
| `startup_timeout_sec` | Maximum time to wait for server to start | 10 |

This aligns with other MCP client implementations:
- **OpenAI Codex** supports `tool_timeout_sec` and `startup_timeout_sec`
- **LM Studio** supports `timeout` in milliseconds
- **Java MCP SDK** supports `.requestTimeout(Duration)`

## Use Case

We have an MCP server (DevGenie) that performs parallel code reviews by spawning child agents. Each child agent calls `GetRulesFromBatch` tool. If this tool hangs or takes too long, the entire review process stalls with no recovery mechanism.

With timeout configuration, we could:
1. Set a 10-second timeout for batch processing tools
2. Have the agent receive a timeout error and handle it gracefully
3. Implement retry logic or fallback to sequential processing

## Environment

- VS Code Version: Latest
- Copilot Extension Version: Latest
- OS: Windows 11

## Related Issues

- #13122 - MCP Servers Stop Working After Copilot Agent Prompts

## Additional Context

The MCP protocol itself doesn't mandate timeout behavior, leaving it to client implementations. Adding this configuration would give developers control over tool execution boundaries and improve reliability of agent-based workflows.

unique_issues.title: Allow specifying the model for subagents in runSubagent
unique_issues.body:
### Problem

When using agent mode, the `runSubagent` tool spawns subagents that always inherit the model currently selected in the main Copilot model dropdown. There is no way to specify a different model for subagents.

### Proposed Solution

Add an optional `model` parameter to the `runSubagent` tool, for example:

```json
{
  "prompt": "...",
  "description": "...",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4.6"
}
```

If omitted, the current behavior (inherit the main model) would be preserved. When specified, the subagent would use the requested model (subject to the user's subscription/plan).

### Use Cases

- **Model specialization:** Use a fast/cheap model for simple lookups and a stronger model for complex reasoning within the same agent session.
- **Cost control:** Delegate simple subtasks to lighter models while keeping the main agent on a premium model, saving quota.
- **Diversity of thought:** Dispatch the same question to multiple different models in parallel and synthesize their varied perspectives for more robust answers.

unique_issues.title: Claude Agent integration opens 3 blank VS Code windows when Anthropic extension starts a session
unique_issues.body:
## Summary

When opening a Claude Code session from the Anthropic VS Code extension (`claude-code`), GitHub Copilot Chat spawns **3 blank "Welcome" VS Code windows**. This happens on every session start and is reproducible 100% of the time.

## Environment

- **VS Code**: 1.98.x (Windows 10 Pro)
- **Copilot Chat extension**: v0.38.2
- **Anthropic Claude Code extension**: latest
- **OS**: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045

## Root Cause Analysis

Copilot Chat v0.38.2 registers **3 separate chat providers** for the `claude-code` session type:
1. `createChatParticipant`
2. `registerChatSessionContentProvider`
3. `createChatSessionItemController`

When the Anthropic extension creates a `claude-code` session, VS Code broadcasts `onChatSession:claude-code`. Each of the 3 provider registrations triggers a new window context, resulting in 3 blank "Welcome" windows.

### Extension Host Logs

The extension host logs show `onChatSession:claude-code` activation events firing 3 times — once per provider registration — each spawning a separate window.

## Workaround

Setting `"github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.enabled": false` in VS Code settings mitigates the issue but disables Copilot's Claude Agent feature entirely.

Removing `"github.copilot.chat.cli.sessionController.enabled": true` alone does **not** resolve the issue.

## Suggested Fix

- Guard session provider registrations to **reuse existing window context** instead of creating new ones
- Don't register for the `claude-code` session type when the session originates from the Anthropic extension (not from Copilot's own Claude Agent feature)
- Alternatively, deduplicate `onChatSession` activation so multiple provider registrations within the same extension don't each spawn a new window

## Reproduction Steps

1. Install both GitHub Copilot Chat and the Anthropic Claude Code VS Code extension
2. Ensure `github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.enabled` is `true` (default)
3. Open a Claude Code session from the Anthropic extension (panel or terminal)
4. Observe 3 blank "Welcome" VS Code windows spawning

unique_issues.title: VS Code Sessions UI hangs indefinitely when MCP tool returns large response (~100KB)
unique_issues.body:
When an MCP tool returns a large response (~100KB), the VS Code Sessions (Insiders) UI shows a loading state that never resolves. The data is returned successfully by the MCP server — the Copilot CLI in the terminal can access and display it — but the Sessions UI never renders the result.

Steps to Reproduce
Open VS Code Sessions (Insiders)
Invoke an MCP tool that returns a large dataset (e.g., a tool returning ~95 rows of tabular data in markdown format, totaling ~100KB)
Observe the UI shows a loading indicator that never completes
Expected Behavior
The response should render in the UI, or if too large, the UI should display a meaningful error/warning (e.g., "Response too large to display — showing first N results") rather than loading indefinitely.

Actual Behavior
The UI shows an infinite loading state. No data, no error, no timeout.

Additional Context
The same MCP tool call works perfectly in the Copilot CLI terminal — data is returned and accessible
The CLI logs the response as "Output too large to read at once (100.2 KB)" and saves to a temp file, confirming the data is received
Filtering/pagination at the MCP server level is a workaround, but the UI should handle large responses gracefully
Extension version: github.copilot-chat-0.40.2026031004
OS: Windows

unique_issues.title: Feature request: Add newChat option to agent handoffs and a command to invoke prompt files programmatically
unique_issues.body:
## Problem

When building multi-agent workflows with custom agents (`.agent.md`), handoffs always continue in the **same chat session**. For long, multi-step workflows this causes real problems:

1. **Context window saturation** — By step 5 of a 7-step workflow, the context window is heavily loaded with prior conversation history from steps 1–4. The agent has less effective working memory for the current task.
2. **No clean separation of concerns** — Each step produces file-based artifacts that the next agent reads from disk. The in-memory conversation history is redundant and sometimes contradictory (e.g., earlier drafts that were revised).
3. **No way to programmatically start a fresh session** — Prompt files (`.prompt.md`) already encode per-step instructions with the correct `agent`, `model`, and `tools`, but there's no mechanism to invoke them automatically from a handoff or hook.

## Real-World Use Case

I maintain [azure-agentic-infraops](https://github.com/jonathan-vella/azure-agentic-infraops), a multi-agent system with 14 agents spanning a 7-step workflow for Azure infrastructure:

```
Requirements → Architecture → Design → Governance → IaC Plan → IaC Code → Deploy → As-Built Docs
```

Each agent writes artifacts to `agent-output/{project}/` and the next agent reads them from disk. We have 18 prompt files (`/step0-kickoff`, `/step1-requirements`, `/step2-architecture`, etc.) that perfectly encode each step's agent, model, and instructions. But there's no way to chain them across fresh chat sessions.

By the time we reach Step 5 (IaC Code Generation), the context window has accumulated 4+ prior steps worth of conversation. The code generation agent would perform significantly better with a clean context that only includes its own instructions plus the artifact files on disk.

## Proposed Solutions (any of these would work)

### Option A: `newChat` field in handoff schema

Add an optional `newChat: boolean` field to the `handoffs:` frontmatter:

```yaml
handoffs:
  - label: "Step 5: Generate Bicep"
    agent: 06b-Bicep CodeGen
    prompt: "Implement Bicep templates per agent-output/{project}/04-implementation-plan.md"
    send: true
    newChat: true  # ← Opens a new chat session with the target agent
```

### Option B: VS Code command to run a prompt file

Expose a command like `copilot.chat.runPrompt` that opens a new chat and invokes a specific `.prompt.md`:

```jsonc
// Could be used from hooks, keybindings, or tasks
{
  "command": "copilot.chat.runPrompt",
  "args": { "prompt": "step5b-bicep-codegen", "newChat": true }
}
```

This would also enable hooks (e.g., the `Stop` lifecycle event) to chain to the next step.

### Option C: `chat.promptFilesRecommendations` with agent awareness

The existing `chat.promptFilesRecommendations` setting shows prompts when starting a new chat, but it could be smarter — surface the **most relevant next prompt** based on the last active agent. For example, after `05b-Bicep Planner` finishes, a new chat could prominently suggest `/step5b-bicep-codegen`.

## Current Workaround

Users must manually:
1. Open a new chat
2. Select the correct agent from the picker
3. Type `/step5b-bicep-codegen` or paste the handoff prompt

This breaks the flow and is error-prone for non-technical users following the workflow.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.111.0
- OS: Linux (dev container) / Windows / macOS
- Copilot Extension: Latest

unique_issues.title: MCP servers with autoStart:true in mcp.json do not auto-start
unique_issues.body:
## Bug Report

### Environment
- **VS Code version**: Latest (March 2026)
- **OS**: macOS (Apple Silicon / arm64)
- **MCP config location**: `~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/mcp.json`

### Problem
MCP servers configured in the user-level `mcp.json` file with `"autoStart": true` do **not** auto-start when VS Code launches or when a new chat session begins.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure MCP servers in `~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/mcp.json` with `"autoStart": true`
2. Set `"chat.mcp.autostart": "always"` in `settings.json`
3. Reload / restart VS Code
4. Open a new Copilot chat session

### Expected Behavior
MCP servers should auto-start and their tools should be available to Copilot immediately in any chat session.

### Actual Behavior
- Servers show as **"Stopped"** in "MCP: List Servers"
- MCP tools are **not available** to Copilot agent
- Users must manually start each server via "MCP: List Servers" every time
- The servers work perfectly fine when tested directly via terminal (stdio JSON-RPC handshake succeeds)

### Additional Context
- The servers respond correctly to JSON-RPC `initialize` when tested via terminal
- This defeats the purpose of `autoStart: true` and `chat.mcp.autostart: "always"`
- Users expect a "configure once, works everywhere" experience for MCP servers

### Workaround
Running the MCP tool binary directly from terminal as a fallback, bypassing the MCP server integration entirely.

unique_issues.title: Add native /context usage breakdown for context window visibility
unique_issues.body: ### What variant of Codex are you using? CLI / TUI ### What feature would you like to see? I would like to propose a read-only /context command in the Codex TUI that shows a native-style context usage card. The command would help users inspect how the current context window is being used during a session. In workflows that use MCP servers, tools, or skills, it is not always easy to tell how much of the available context window is being used by system prompt content, system tools, MCP tool schemas, skill-related context, regular messages, or remaining free space. The proposed /context card would show the current context window composition across these categories: - System prompt - System tools - MCP tools - Skills - Messages - Free space The command would support a compact default view through /context and a fuller breakdown through /context full. The goal is to provide a lightweight inspection surface that helps users understand what is currently occupying the context window, without changing request construction, conversation history, model behavior, or provider-side usage accounting. This proposal is not intended to change provider-side usage accounting, rate limit behavior, context compaction behavior, tool or skill injection policy, or request construction semantics. It is intended only as a native visibility and inspection feature. A focused implementation can stay inside the native Codex codebase. It can include the core /context feature, native context usage bucket accounting, compact and full slash command routing, TUI rendering, and relevant in-repo tests or snapshots needed to keep the behavior stable. The command should remain read-only. It should not mutate the live session, should not add messages to the conversation, and should not change the next request. ### Additional information I attached two screenshots below to show the proposed TUI shape: Default compact /context view: Full /context view: For the initial upstream PR, I would keep the submitted changes focused on the native feature implementation and the relevant in-repo tests or snapshots. During development, I also checked the accounting model against request-shaped context data to make sure the displayed buckets align with how the context is assembled. I do not think that external validation harness needs to be part of the clean feature PR by default. If maintainers think additional validation details, test cases, or validation scripts would be useful or acceptable for upstream review, I would be happy to provide them or adapt the PR accordingly. This proposal is related to context visibility and usage inspection discussions such as: #26845 #27244 #24403 If this direction looks aligned with Codex’s roadmap, I would be happy to open a focused PR.

### What issue are you seeing?

Compaction repeatedly preserves large image payloads, reducing available context

In the latest compaction window (242), the preserved history contains 66 images whose combined image_url payload size is approximately 49.9 MB.

Codex 0.146 limits compacted text to a 64K token budget, but images appear to be counted as zero tokens while still being preserved alongside user messages.

As a result, every compaction carries the same old images forward again. The image payload continues occupying the preserved context, while the usable space for new messages gradually becomes smaller after each compaction.

Expected behavior:
Images should either be included in the compaction budget, deduplicated, summarized, or removed when they are no longer required.
Actual behavior:
Old image payloads are repeatedly preserved without affecting the token calculation, causing progressive context-space exhaustion.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Compaction retains historical images and leaves progressively less context

  Codex CLI 0.146.0 repeatedly preserves full base64 input_image data inside compacted replacement_history.

  Measured in one session:

  - Compactions: 242
  - Retained images: 66
  - Latest compacted record: 50.2 MB
  - Rollout file: 8.1 GB
  - Context left after compaction decreased from approximately 35% to 15%, then 10%

  compact_remote_v2.rs counts images as zero tokens but still retains them. This causes context and disk usage to grow after every compaction.

  Expected: old images should be removed, summarized or replaced with lightweight references during compaction.

### What is the expected behavior?

unique_issues.title: CLI MCP login fails for Grafana Cloud MCP because OAuth probe omits MCP Accept header
unique_issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.147.0

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

`codex mcp login grafana` fails during OAuth metadata discovery for Grafana Cloud's hosted MCP server with the following error:

```
Error: Metadata error: OAuth metadata discovery failed for https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp
  Caused by: OAuth discovery redirect to non-same-origin URL rejected:
  https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/machine-learning/assistant/configure/cloud-mcp/
```

The reason is that `codex mcp login` performs its initial probe without the Accept header. It encounters the redirect to grafana.com and correctly rejects that cross-origin redirect during security-sensitive OAuth discovery.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

- `codex mcp add --url https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp grafana`
- `codex mcp login grafana`


### What is the expected behavior?

`codex mcp login` proceeds with metadata discovery and launches the OAuth authorization process.


### Additional information

Grafana currently behaves like this:

- Plain GET https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp → 302 redirect to Grafana documentation.
- The same request with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream → correct 401 OAuth challenge.
- Grafana’s OAuth metadata endpoints themselves return valid JSON.

`codex mcp login` performs its initial probe without the MCP Accept header. It encounters the redirect to
grafana.com and correctly rejects that cross-origin redirect during security-sensitive OAuth discovery.

A plain request reproduces the redirect:

```shell
curl -I https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp
# HTTP 302, Location: https://grafana.com/docs/...
```

When the MCP Accept header is supplied, Grafana returns the expected OAuth challenge:

```shell
curl -I \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp
# HTTP 401
# WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.grafana.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/
mcp"
```

The proper fix is for Codex’s OAuth discovery probe to send the MCP accept types.

Workaround:

```toml
[mcp_servers.grafana]
url = "https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp"
http_headers = {
  "X-Grafana-URL" = "https://your-stack.grafana.net",
  "Accept" = "application/json, text/event-stream"
}
```

unique_issues.title: MCP OAuth cannot send pre-registered client_secret for Google Workspace MCP
unique_issues.body:
## Summary

Codex can complete the Google OAuth authorization flow for Google Workspace MCP, but the token exchange fails because no OAuth client secret is sent:

```
OAuth token exchange failed:
invalid_request: client_secret is missing
```

Google Workspace MCP's official configuration uses a Google **Web OAuth client** and requires both `client_id` and `client_secret`.

## Environment

- ChatGPT app: `26.803.41515`
- Bundled Codex CLI: `0.147.0-alpha.6.5`
- MCP endpoint: `https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Google Workspace/Gmail MCP endpoint in Codex.
2. Configure the pre-registered OAuth `client_id` (the current documented per-server OAuth setting).
3. Run the MCP OAuth login flow.
4. Complete the Google authorization screen, account selection, and scope consent.
5. Observe that the callback contains `iss=https://accounts.google.com`.
6. Observe the token exchange error:

```
OAuth token exchange failed:
invalid_request: client_secret is missing
```

The previous error, `Authorization server response missing required issuer`, no longer occurs in this environment.

## Expected behavior

Codex should support a secure per-MCP-server configuration for a pre-registered/confidential OAuth client, including `client_secret`, and send it to the token endpoint as required by the provider. The secret should be handled through an appropriate secure local/app credential store rather than exposed in logs.

## Actual behavior

The available/documented MCP OAuth configuration exposes `client_id`, but I could not find a supported per-server `client_secret` setting in the current CLI/App configuration. As a result, Google rejects the authorization-code token exchange.

Google's official MCP setup documentation requires a Web OAuth client with both values:
https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/configure-mcp-servers?hl=en

## Related issues

- RFC 9207 issuer handling: #31573
- Google Workspace MCP reports: #34427, #34684
- Pre-registered/static OAuth client identity: #19154
- Slack MCP requiring a pre-registered client identity: #13200
- Related MCP OAuth configuration discussion: #35253

## Request

Please add support for pre-registered OAuth client credentials for remote MCP servers (at minimum a secure `client_secret` path), or document an official supported workaround for providers such as Google Workspace MCP that require a confidential Web OAuth client.

unique_issues.title: Customizable Session Background / Context Window Colors
unique_issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

GUI App

### What feature would you like to see?

Description

Please add an option to customize the visual appearance of individual Codex sessions or context windows, such as:

Background color
Accent/window color
Optional background image

A good reference for this functionality is Windows Terminal, where different terminal profiles can have distinct colors, themes, or background images.

Ideally, these appearance settings could be configured per project, workspace, or session.

Motivation

This would make it much easier to visually distinguish between different projects when switching between Codex sessions.

When several sessions are open at the same time, their interfaces currently look very similar. It is therefore quite easy to switch to the wrong session and accidentally enter a prompt or reply that was intended for another project.

For example:

Project A could use a blue background.
Project B could use a dark green background.
Project C could use a custom background image or accent color.

The visual difference would provide an immediate indication of which project/session is currently active, without needing to repeatedly check the session title or context.

Benefits
Reduces accidental prompts being sent to the wrong project/session.
Makes switching between multiple active Codex sessions much safer and faster.
Provides an immediate visual indication of the current project context.
Particularly useful for users working across several repositories or projects simultaneously.
Possible Implementation

Similar to Windows Terminal profiles, Codex could allow appearance settings to be associated with a project or session, for example:

Appearance
├── Background color
├── Accent color
├── Background image
├── Background image opacity
└── Use project-specific appearance

Even basic support for assigning a different background or accent color to each project would already make a significant difference.

unique_issues.title: codex mcp add / mcp remove rewrite every [mcp_servers.*] entry, silently dropping comments and unknown keys
unique_issues.body:
### What happens

`codex mcp add` rewrites **every** existing `[mcp_servers.*]` entry in `config.toml`, not just the one being added. Anything this build does not model is dropped on the way through, and so is the surrounding formatting.

Environment: `codex-cli 0.154.0`, Windows 11 (10.0.26200).

### Reproduction

1. Start from a hand-written config:

```toml
# TOP COMMENT must survive
model = "gpt-5.6-luna"

# MCP SECTION COMMENT must survive
[mcp_servers.alpha]
command = "npx"                # inline comment A
args = ["-y", "alpha-server"]
startup_timeout_sec = 30
tool_timeout_sec = 120
enabled = false
future_unknown_key = "keep-me"

[mcp_servers.alpha.env]
ALPHA_KEY = "1"

[mcp_servers.alpha.tools.dangerous_tool]
approval_mode = "approve"

[mcp_servers.beta]
url = "https://example.com/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "BETA_TOKEN"

[mcp_servers.beta.env_http_headers]
X-Tenant = "TENANT_ENV"
```

2. Run an unrelated command:

```console
$ codex mcp add gamma -- npx -y gamma
Added global MCP server 'gamma'.
```

3. The resulting config:

```toml
# TOP COMMENT must survive
model = "gpt-5.6-luna"

[mcp_servers.alpha]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "alpha-server"]
enabled = false
startup_timeout_sec = 30.0
tool_timeout_sec = 120.0

[mcp_servers.alpha.env]
ALPHA_KEY = "1"

[mcp_servers.alpha.tools.dangerous_tool]
approval_mode = "approve"

[mcp_servers.beta]
url = "https://example.com/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "BETA_TOKEN"

[mcp_servers.beta.env_http_headers]
X-Tenant = "TENANT_ENV"

[mcp_servers.gamma]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "gamma"]
```

### Expected vs actual

Expected: `gamma` is added; `alpha` and `beta` are untouched.

Actual, deleted or altered in the two untouched entries:

* `# MCP SECTION COMMENT must survive` - gone.
* `# inline comment A` - gone.
* `future_unknown_key = "keep-me"` - gone. Any key this build does not recognise is silently removed.
* `startup_timeout_sec = 30` -> `30.0`, `tool_timeout_sec = 120` -> `120.0`.
* Key order changes (`enabled` moves above the timeouts).

Values that are modelled survive intact: `env`, `env_http_headers`, `tools.<name>.approval_mode`, `bearer_token_env_var`, `enabled = false`.

### Root cause

Two halves of the same round-trip:

1. `load_global_mcp_servers` deserializes the table into `BTreeMap<String, McpServerConfig>` (`codex-rs/config/src/mcp_edit.rs:19-31`). `McpServerConfig` (`codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:207-279`) keeps no representation of unrecognised keys, so they are discarded on load.
2. `replace_mcp_servers` then replaces each existing entry with a freshly serialized table (`codex-rs/core/src/config/edit.rs:469-479`), which discards the `toml_edit` decor (comments, whitespace, original scalar formatting) attached to that item. Only entries that are new or changed need rewriting; unchanged ones are rewritten anyway.

The same code path is used by `codex mcp remove` (`codex-rs/cli/src/mcp_cmd.rs:487-491`) and by `codex mcp login`, so any of those commands will do this to the whole `[mcp_servers]` table.

### Impact

* Comments and formatting in `[mcp_servers.*]` are lost, so annotations such as "disabled because the token rotates weekly" disappear without warning, and the diff for a one-line change is the entire section.
* Unknown keys are deleted permanently. This bites whenever the config is touched by more than one Codex build - for example a Desktop-bundled CLI and a separately installed npm CLI - because the older build removes keys the newer one wrote.
* Silent: nothing is printed, and the command exits 0.

Related but distinct: #36844 (config rewrite drops the BOM) is another case of the rewrite not preserving what it did not model.

### Possible fix

Edit the `toml_edit` document in place and only touch the entry being added or removed, leaving all other entries as raw `toml::Value` instead of round-tripping them through the typed model. If unknown keys must be dropped, doing it explicitly with a warning would at least be visible.

Happy to provide the before/after files and an exact command sequence if that helps.

unique_issues.title: [Windows] Sandbox: Access denied on existing workspace descendants after sandbox SID change
unique_issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.908.40834

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (5x)

### What platform is your computer?

 Win32NT 10.0.19045.0 Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 10.0.19045.0 True

### What issue are you seeing?

### Summary

After a Codex sandbox re-initialization changed the sandbox user's SID, the sandbox lost write access to files inside existing subdirectories of the workspace. Codex cannot patch, edit, or generate code in any project with an established file tree.

### Symptoms

- Codex reports PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied when writing to existing files.
- The apply_patch tool reports "path contains a reparse point" — this is a false positive, verified with fsutil reparsepoint query, which returns "The file or directory is not a reparse point".
- The failure is reproducible for the entire subtree of apps/api/app, while apps/api (parent) and apps/web/src work fine.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045.0 x64)
- Codex App (Windows), version 26.908.40834
- Subscription: ChatGPT Pro
- Sandbox user (whoami): desktop-583kd57\codexsandboxoffline
- Sandbox user current SID: S-1-5-21-1747488710-827246756-3187947173-1006

### Diagnostics

- whoami returns desktop-583kd57\codexsandboxoffline.
- The current sandbox user's SID (resolved from whoami via NTAccount.Translate) is S-1-5-21-1747488710-827246756-3187947173-1006.
- icacls on apps/api and apps/api/app both show the group CodexSandboxUsers with inheritable (OI)(CI)(M).
- However, the sandbox user's current SID is present in apps/api's ACL but absent from apps/api/app's ACL, despite inheritable ACEs on the parent.
- AreAccessRulesProtected is False on both paths, so inheritance is not blocked at the ACL level.
- Reboot did not resolve the issue.
- Manually granting the current SID resolves it permanently for that path (212 files updated, 0 failed).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up Codex on Windows with the default sandbox.
2. Work in a repository with an existing directory structure and files.
3. Force a sandbox re-initialization (app update, or sandbox state reset).
4. In Codex, attempt to edit any file under apps/api/app/mirigdkp_api/.
5. The write fails with Access is denied.

### Expected Behavior

The sandbox should either:
- recursively repair ACLs on all existing workspace files when the SID changes, or
- fail loudly at startup with an actionable error, or
- automatically request elevated permission to repair ACLs when it detects the sandbox user cannot write.

Currently none of these happen: Codex silently loses the ability to edit parts of the workspace, and the only fix is a manual icacls command run by the user.

### Workaround

Run elevated PowerShell and execute:
icacls "C:\path\to\workspace\subdir" /grant "*S-1-5-21-1747488710-827246756-3187947173-1006:(OI)(CI)(M)" /t /c /q

This restores write access until the next sandbox SID change.

### Related Issues

- #15165 (Windows elevated sandbox does not recursively grant usable ACLs to existing workspace files)
- #28943 (Fix Windows sandbox runtime ACL refresh) — fixed runtime binaries but not workspace descendants.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Set up Codex on Windows with the default elevated sandbox, working in a repository with an existing directory tree and existing files (e.g. C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app\mirigdkp_api\).

2. Use Codex normally for several sessions. Writes work fine at first.

3. Trigger a sandbox re-initialization. Any of these does it:
   - Codex App update
   - Rebooting Windows
   - Sandbox state reset

4. In a new Codex session, ask it to edit a file inside an existing subdirectory, for example:
   apps/api/app/mirigdkp_api/api/epoch_lifecycle.py

5. Codex reports:
   - PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied
   - apply_patch: "path contains a reparse point"
   (the reparse point message is a false positive — fsutil reparsepoint query returns "The file or directory is not a reparse point")

6. Reproduce the boundary with manual commands in PowerShell:

   Set-Content "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\__test.tmp" -Value "x"
   Remove-Item "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\__test.tmp"
   -> succeeds

   Set-Content "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app\__test.tmp" -Value "x"
   Remove-Item "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app\__test.tmp"
   -> Access is denied

   Set-Content "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\web\src\__test.tmp" -Value "x"
   Remove-Item "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\web\src\__test.tmp"
   -> succeeds

7. Confirm the SID boundary with icacls:

   icacls "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api" | Select-String "1747488710-827246756-3187947173"
   -> the sandbox user's current SID is present

   icacls "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app" | Select-String "1747488710-827246756-3187947173"
   -> the sandbox user's current SID is absent

8. Check inheritance:

   (Get-Acl "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api").AreAccessRulesProtected        -> False
   (Get-Acl "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app").AreAccessRulesProtected    -> False

   So inheritance is not blocked, CodexSandboxUsers has (OI)(CI)(M) on both directories, but the sandbox user's own SID is not propagated to the descendant directories.

9. Confirm the fix:

   icacls "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app" /grant "*S-1-5-21-1747488710-827246756-3187947173-1006:(OI)(CI)(M)" /t /c /q
   -> 212 files processed, 0 failed. Writes now succeed. But the fix is lost when the sandbox SID changes again.

### What is the expected behavior?

When the sandbox user's SID changes, the elevated sandbox setup should either:

(a) recursively repair ACLs on all existing workspace descendants under the write roots, not just at the top level, OR

(b) fail loudly at startup with a clear, actionable error, telling the user what went wrong and how to fix it, OR

(c) automatically elevate and repair ACLs when it detects that the current sandbox user cannot write to a path it is expected to own.

Currently none of these happens. Codex silently loses the ability to edit parts of the workspace, and the only remedy is a manual icacls command that has to be repeated after every sandbox SID change.

Expected minimal behavior: if the sandbox detects it cannot write to a path under a configured write root, it should not proceed with a patch operation that will only fail with Access is denied. It should report the problem before the user invests effort in a task.

### Additional information

### Diagnostics from a real case

- Codex App version: 26.908.40834 (Windows)
- Platform: Windows 10 (10.0.19045.0 x64)
- Subscription: ChatGPT Pro
- Sandbox user (whoami): desktop-583kd57\codexsandboxoffline
- Sandbox user current SID: S-1-5-21-1747488710-827246756-3187947173-1006

### Failure boundary

- Workspace root: C:\MiriGDKPv2
- Writes succeed: C:\MiriGDKPv2, C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps, C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api, C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\web\src
- Writes fail: C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app, C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app\mirigdkp_api, and all their descendants

The boundary matches exactly where the sandbox user's current SID is absent from the ACL, even though the parent directory has inheritable ACEs that should have propagated down.

### ACL evidence

icacls "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api" shows (abbreviated):
  DESKTOP-583KD57\CodexSandboxUsers:(OI)(CI)(M)
  S-1-5-21-1747488710-...-1006:(I)(OI)(CI)(M)   <- current sandbox SID, present here
  NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)
  ...

icacls "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app" shows the same set EXCEPT the sandbox user's current SID S-1-5-21-1747488710-...-1006 is absent.

Get-Acl confirms: AreAccessRulesProtected = False on both paths (inheritance is not blocked).

### What did NOT help

- Reboot: did not repair the ACLs, the failure persisted across reboot.
- Attempting to write via Copy-Item instead of Set-Content: same error (CopyFileInfoItemUnauthorizedAccessError).
- fsutil reparsepoint query on the target file: "The file or directory is not a reparse point." (Confirms the apply_patch error message is misleading.)

### What DID work

Running an elevated PowerShell and executing:

  icacls "C:\MiriGDKPv2\apps\api\app" /grant "*S-1-5-21-1747488710-827246756-3187947173-1006:(OI)(CI)(M)" /t /c /q

Result: "Successfully processed 212 files; Failed processing 0 files." Writes restored until the next sandbox SID change.

### Related issues

- #31888 (Windows: workspace-write sandbox blocks apply_patch with EPERM on %USERPROFILE%) — different scope: that's about writes outside the workspace; this is about writes inside the workspace, in existing descendants.
- #15165 (Windows elevated sandbox does not recursively grant usable ACLs to existing workspace files) — likely related root cause but different symptom set.
- #28943 (Fix Windows sandbox runtime ACL refresh) — fixed runtime binaries, not workspace descendants.

### Impact

This breaks Codex on any Windows project with an established file tree. For a user who has been working in the same repository for weeks, the sandbox silently loses write access to most of the codebase. The user has to manually fix ACLs after every sandbox re-initialization, which they may not realize until Codex fails mid-task.
