unique_issues.title: Windows sandbox leaks kernel access tokens (~33 per sandboxed command; paged pool grows until reboot)
unique_issues.body:
### What happens
On Windows 11, each command that the Codex CLI runs inside its Windows sandbox leaks kernel access-token objects. Paged pool tag `Toke` (with `SeAt`, `SeTd` and `SeDt` scaling alongside it) grows for as long as sandboxed commands run. It is never reclaimed until a full Restart. With Fast Startup on, "Shut down" hibernates the kernel and keeps the leak.

No user-mode process holds the tokens: the highest handle count system-wide is about 6k. So they appear to be kernel references that the sandbox's restricted-token / command-runner path never releases.

### Reproduction
1. Read the `Toke` pool tag's live allocation count. We used NtQuerySystemInformation with SystemPoolTagInformation (class 22), which works without elevation; PoolMon gives the same number.
2. Run 20 sandboxed no-op commands:
   ```powershell
   1..20 | ForEach-Object { codex sandbox -- cmd /c exit 0 }
   ```
3. Read the `Toke` count again.

### Measurements (Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, codex-cli 0.160.1)
| Run | Toke live delta |
|---|---|
| 20 × `codex sandbox -- cmd /c exit 0` | +918 in 43 s (about 33 per command above baseline) |
| 100 × plain `python -c pass` spawns, no sandbox | at baseline |
| idle, no `codex-command-runner` alive | +107 in 60 s (an unrelated background rate) |

After about 18 hours of normal agent use: `Toke` was 1,692 MB of paged pool with 770k live allocations. A second machine (Windows 11 Home, 16 GB) showed the same signature: 1,360 MB `Toke` and 655k allocations. That came to about 1.7 GB of paged pool before a restart.

### Expected
Sandboxed commands release their token references when the command exits, and paged pool stays flat.

### Workaround
Restart (not Shut down) regularly, or turn off Fast Startup so Shut down clears kernel pool.

unique_issues.title: Expose trusted resolved execution context to policy hooks
unique_issues.body:
# Trusted resolved execution context for policy hooks

Tracking use case: erickb336/sage#243. This request concerns a supported runtime contract for policy extensions. It is separate from required-hook failure handling in #41979.

Related reports: #32360 and #50271 cover effective working directory; #40996 covers permission context. This request brings those needs together with executor identity, filesystem namespace, shell resolution, and per-call freshness. If an existing supported interface covers them, please point us to it.

## Problem

A policy hook needs the settings that the executor will actually use. Original model arguments do not establish those settings. A hook cannot safely infer execution paths from its own environment when a command selects a different working directory, shell, or remote executor.

In rust-v0.162.1, the exec_command PreToolUse payload contains the command string. The hook cwd uses the local environment cwd, with the turn cwd as fallback. These fields do not attest the pending command's resolved execution context.

Sources checked:
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec/exec_command.rs#L514
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L609
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs#L248

## Requested capability

Provide a supported, versioned policy interface for the resolved operation before execution. An extension to an existing hook or a separate runtime callback could satisfy this request. The interface must bind evidence to the authenticated session, actor, turn, and exact tool call.

Required evidence or equivalent trusted checks:

- Selected executor and filesystem namespace, including whether execution is local or remote.
- Effective working directory after resolving omitted, empty, relative, and explicit inputs.
- Effective shell executable, shell type, and invocation/login behavior.
- The lookup settings needed for executable and path policy, including PATH, HOME, and CDPATH, without exposing credentials or a full environment dump.
- Effective sandbox and permission policy, including permitted additions and inherited settings.
- A supported way to evaluate relevant filesystem, symlink, executable identity, and checkout evidence in that same namespace.

Specify when evidence is captured, how rewrites affect it, and what invalidates an earlier decision. A changed executor, directory, permission setting, or operation must require a fresh decision. Evidence for one call must not authorize another. Successful extension policy must preserve native sandbox and approval checks.

The interface must state its limits. Shell startup scripts and arbitrary programs can change behavior after this point. Context metadata is not proof that a command is harmless and does not replace a filesystem sandbox.

## Validation examples

1. Compare omitted and explicit workdir inputs with the command's actual directory in an isolated fixture.
2. Compare requested shell strings with the runtime-selected executable and invocation.
3. Exercise inherited and explicit permission settings without bypassing native approvals.
4. Verify local and remote namespaces; local filesystem inspection must not stand in for remote evidence.
5. Refuse mismatched session, actor, turn, or call identities, stale snapshots, and changed operations.
6. Verify denial prevents the operation. Separately cover hook timeout, exception, and transport failure through the fail-closed contract.

## Current Sage boundary

Sage can recover original requested arguments from protected native transcripts. Its verified fixture path does not establish a complete installed evaluator. Automatic activation remains disabled. Native probes with simulated model responses establish only the behavior they directly observe.

## Evidence limits

The source audit covers rust-v0.162.1. At submission, rust-v0.163.0 is the latest published release; it has not been source-audited or native-tested in this investigation. The cited 0.162.1 source was read directly. This request does not claim a new native comparison run or that every possible runtime interface was exhaustively excluded.

Sage needs a supported producer or a separately designed execution boundary. Model-supplied fields cannot supply runtime authority.

unique_issues.title: MCP OAuth: optionally redirect to a landing page the MCP server provides after sign-in
unique_issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

CLI 0.163.0 (Linux, x86_64): remote MCP servers added with `codex mcp add <name> --url https://…` that sign in through `codex-rmcp-client`.

### What feature would you like to see?

An option for the MCP server to choose where the browser ends up after its OAuth sign-in.

Today the browser finishes on the local callback listener (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback/<id>`). #36915 asks to bring that page in line with the Codex login UX, and we support it. This request is the separate part #36915 leaves out on purpose: after the authorization code has been exchanged for tokens successfully, the listener answers with a `303` to a landing URL the MCP server advertises. The flow then ends on the server's own "connected" screen, which can name the workspace and the access that was granted, things Codex cannot know. Codex keeps its own page whenever the server advertises nothing or anything about the URL is in doubt.

There is no standard field for this today. One option is an extension field in the authorization server metadata (RFC 8414 allows extension parameters), for example `post_authorization_landing_uri`. A field agreed in the MCP specification would serve every client, and we are happy to raise it there.

Constraints we would expect:

- `https` only, and the same origin as the authorization server's `issuer`. Codex never sends the user to a third party.
- The redirect carries no `code`, no `state` and no token, nothing from the exchange. At most it carries a fixed `result=success`.
- It is followed only after the token exchange succeeds. A failed exchange keeps Codex's own error page.
- Any parse failure or origin mismatch falls back silently to the built-in page.

### Additional information

Why it matters: for a user, the browser step is the MCP server's sign-in. The tab they were in a moment earlier was the server's own approval page, so a client page that names neither the server nor the account reads to them as an error from the server's product. A server landing page keeps the whole step in one voice without changing OAuth discovery, scopes, callback validation or the token exchange.

The same request is being filed with Claude Code, so a shared field in the MCP specification would be the natural home for it.

unique_issues.title: Severe UI reasoning failures: basic interaction defects missed despite successful workflow tests
unique_issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

I am fucking furious with the quality of the work and, especially, the agent's judgment about its own output.

Codex generated two native UI implementations for the same task and presented runnable workflows and successful tests while missing elementary interaction failures. This report concerns Codex's generation, reasoning, and self-evaluation: the defective controls described below are in the application it generated.

The task was an appearance editor where users converse with an agent, see the current visual result, and decide whether to apply it. The observed problems were:

- The visual preview scrolls away with the conversation. As messages accumulate, the object being edited disappears from view.
- Sent messages look like editable text fields or unstructured text, surrounded by redundant, persistent status descriptions.
- In the presented state, version B's send icon is effectively invisible.
- Version A has a back arrow and a close button; version B has both "Collapse" and close. Their consequences are not clear from the interface.
- "Save and Apply" sits directly beneath the message composer, making it unclear whether the action applies the visual work or saves the typed message.
- The main presentation uses internal English test requests, "Create a visual work" and "Continue the same work," without making their meaning clear to the person reviewing the result.

The supervisor did not catch these as delivery-blocking design problems. I had to ask what the messages meant, what would happen after five requests, and whether the preview would scroll away. Only through that interrogation did the failure of the continuing interaction become explicit.

This is not a request for a different color palette or a matter of personal taste. The agent filled a screen without adequately considering what happens when the person actually uses it over time.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is the observed sequence from one project, not a guaranteed deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Ask Codex to implement and evaluate a continuous visual-editing workflow with a preview, conversation, persistence, and cancellation.
2. Have two independent blank construction sessions receive the same requirements and starting code. In one session, provide a generic mechanism for the builder to define its own page semantics.
3. Let the agents implement, run checks, and present their results. Review the interaction after multiple messages, with the keyboard open, and through sending, applying, and closing.
4. Ask the supervising agent what its experiment actually established. In this case, it acknowledged that visual differences could simply be different design choices and that a real consuming agent had not independently understood and operated the page. The operation probe used a test program, not a natural-language agent making its own decisions.

There was also a concrete operation mismatch: the semantic save path reported completion and saved the work, while the creation page still declared it unsaved and disabled its save button. The agent disclosed this failure, but the overall handoff still did not apply an adequate standard of interaction quality.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should evaluate the complete evolving interaction before presenting a UI as an acceptable result. It should catch ambiguous controls, weak action-to-object relationships, unreadable affordances, repetitive status copy, and loss of the editing context without making the user discover each problem.

It should distinguish "the scripted workflow ran" from "the interface is well designed," and distinguish "a program can read semantic data or invoke an action" from "an agent can understand the page and complete the user's task." A single pair of different designs does not establish that semantics improved construction quality.

Passing tests and producing confident explanations do not make a bad interface good. Stop making me perform the elementary design review that the agent was supposed to own.

Please investigate failures in task understanding, dynamic interaction review, experimental validity, and completion judgment. I want the underlying quality failure investigated, not another reassuring promise to rebuild everything.

### Environment and additional information

- Incident: 19 October 2026, approximately 21:16 SGT (UTC+8).
- Installed desktop app bundle: `com.openai.codex`, version `26.1013.40934`, build `20770`.
- Host: macOS `26.6.2`, arm64; `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`.
- The two external construction sessions used the same configured model and reasoning settings, through bundled CLI `0.163.0-alpha.10.2`.
- This feels like a serious regression in practical reasoning and design judgment. I have not established a measured before/after regression or a server-side model downgrade.
- Private project source, full conversation transcripts, screenshots, and diagnostic logs are not attached to this public issue.

unique_issues.body:
**Component:** Codex app-server daemon 0.163.0 (`codex app-server --remote-control --managed-daemon`, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl) on a Linux VM, serving long-lived threads for the Codex app. Custom provider via a local proxy in Responses-passthrough mode (OpenCodex 2.84.0 — the proxy was NOT restarted during the recovery below, which is part of the evidence). Catalog context window 1,000,000; effective `model_context_window` reported in `token_count` events: 950,000. `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 700000` set in `~/.codex/config.toml`.

**Observed behavior (2026-10-19, two threads on the same server):**

- Both threads reached a terminal `token_count` state of `total_tokens = 950,000` (exactly the window) with `last_tokens = 0`. Every subsequent turn failed with: "Codex ran out of room in the model's context window. Start a new thread or clear earlier history before retrying."
- The threads' real context, measured from the fresh `token_count` events after recovery, was ~143,625 and ~143,129 tokens — about 15% of the window.
- In an earlier episode on a sibling thread, `total_token_usage` behaved as a running sum of per-turn totals since the last compaction, and the baseline stayed pinned at 950,000 across a manual `/compact` (23,043-token summary): the reported total stayed ~1,020,527 while `last_token_usage` was 70,527.
- One affected thread recorded 36 auto-compaction events over its life and still ended up pinned. A healthy control thread on the same server compacted 24 times, never pinned, and has zero context errors.
- **Recovery:** restarting ONLY the app-server daemon (`codex app-server daemon restart`) made both "dead" threads immediately resume work: new `token_count` events with the real ~143k occupancy, zero context errors since, and the client-side context meter (ring) reappeared. No thread restart, no history clearing.

**Interpretation:** the effective context accounting seems to live in the app-server process memory, where it can pin at the window and survive compactions; it is only recomputed from the thread history when the daemon restarts.

**Expected:** context accounting should track the post-compaction baseline / last-turn usage. A thread at ~143k of a 950k window should never be rejected for lack of room, and a compaction (manual or automatic) should reset the baseline in the running server.

**Workaround:** restart the app-server daemon.

Related reports with different facets of the accounting problem: #53741, #49026.

Reported by RHODIZ IT LLC — production homelab running 4 long-lived Codex threads through this daemon.

unique_issues.title: repeated truncation and rereads are causing absurd context consumption
unique_issues.body:
# Summary

I’m repeatedly running into issues where codex asks to read material, only receives part of it and then keeps trying to reread what was cut off - recovery attempts then return too much and get cut off again.

Codex keeps rereading overlapping document sections and search results, using up more context while making little progress on the actual task. It's burning through an unreasonable amount of context and time.

There's several places I'm noticing it:

- Reading command output
- Searching documentation, opening results, etc
- Using the browser and receiving its instructions
- Reading returned research
- Reviewing session history

Code Mode MIGHT be a contributor, but even when disabled features.code_mode=false.. I'm running into the same issues and it's also happening in instances where code mode isn't even being used: direct-command and browser results

# Environment

- Codex: desktop, version 26.1013.40934 & codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2
- OS: macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon M1
- Model settings: `gpt-6-astra`, `tool_mode="code_mode"`
- The example below uses `functions.exec` and nested `tools.exec_command` calls

# Reproduction

#### With Code Mode Enabled
Using three different pieces of text (**Doc A, Doc B and Doc C**) with tool_output_token_limit=20000

1. With code mode, the command below and the output allowance at default, each command creates 25,000 bytes of text.
2. Check the individual command outputs. All three commands finish successfully and produce their complete results.
3. Check the combined result in the next message sent to the model. **The entirety of Doc B result is missing, along with parts of Doc A and Doc C.**
4. Repeat with three smaller results of 11,000 bytes each. All three arrive intact. A single 25,000-byte result also arrives intact.
5. Repeat the larger test, adding `// @exec: {"max_output_tokens": 22000}` as the first line above `const all=[];`


```javascript
const all=[];
all.push(await tools.exec_command({"cmd": "python3 -c 'import sys; s=sys.argv[1]; n=int(sys.argv[2]); a=s+\"_BEGIN\\n\"; m=s+\"_MIDDLE\\n\"; z=s+\"_END\\n\"; k=n-len(a+m+z); print(a+s.lower()*(k//2)+m+s.lower()*(k-k//2)+z,end=\"\")' A 25000"}));
all.push(await tools.exec_command({"cmd": "python3 -c 'import sys; s=sys.argv[1]; n=int(sys.argv[2]); a=s+\"_BEGIN\\n\"; m=s+\"_MIDDLE\\n\"; z=s+\"_END\\n\"; k=n-len(a+m+z); print(a+s.lower()*(k//2)+m+s.lower()*(k-k//2)+z,end=\"\")' B 25000"}));
all.push(await tools.exec_command({"cmd": "python3 -c 'import sys; s=sys.argv[1]; n=int(sys.argv[2]); a=s+\"_BEGIN\\n\"; m=s+\"_MIDDLE\\n\"; z=s+\"_END\\n\"; k=n-len(a+m+z); print(a+s.lower()*(k//2)+m+s.lower()*(k-k//2)+z,end=\"\")' C 25000"}));
for(let i=0;i<all.length;i++)text({id:i,output:all[i].output});
```

```javascript
// @exec: {"max_output_tokens": 22000}
```

```text
Script completed
Wall time 0.3 seconds
Output:

Warning: truncated output (original token count: 18768)
Total output lines: 3
```

All three commands finished and produced their full 25,000 bytes, but the reply sent to the model was cut down to 40,106 bytes—the whole B result was gone, along with parts of A and C. 

# What Happens On The Backend
- Commands finish, but information disappears before the model receives any results
- Changing the requested range still leaves the reply too large, so recovery hits the same problem again
- The problem also appears in direct-command and browser results outside code mode
- Repeated reads and recovery attempts add more overlapping material and spend more turns trying to get information that was already requested

| Attempt | What codex requested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Attempting to ingest material from three separate documents | Cut short |
| 2 | **Doc A** sent by itself | Returned without a cutoff; recovered seven missing headings |
| 3 | **Doc B** sent by itself| Cut short |
| 4 | Remainder of the **Doc B** plus **Doc C** | Cut short |
| 5 | **Doc C** divided into two ranges, both returned together | Cut short again |
| 6 | A smaller section of **Doc C**| Returns without a cutoff |

The six returned replies totaled 212,643 bytes (including repeated material) and this happens without compaction and output allowances varied from 20,000 to 70,000, without an outer allowance override.

#### With Code Mode Disabled

Using features.code_mode=false, sessions still bypass and run through code mode. The model’s own settings took priority and it continued using it anyway. Attemptning features.code_mode.direct_only_tool_namespaces=["functions"] blocks the command, but returns TypeError: tools.exec_command is not a function.

#### Code Mode Not Used At All For Operation

A direct command produced 60,034 bytes, but the next message sent only contained 40,212 bytes, including status information. The middle was missing, and code mode wasn’t involved. And a browser call lost 8,851 bytes of instructions and it's warning changed from “2,213 tokens truncated” to “7 tokens truncated,” even without receiving missing guidance

# Expected Behavior

Adjust code mode so that it can account for how much an entire reply can hold before requesting and returning large amounts of text. If something gets cut off, it should retrieve the missing sections in pieces that fit instead of continuously forcing more oversized requests 

Whenever content is cut off, codex should clearly identify what’s missing and keep the complete result available where possible. That would let it read the missing sections instead of getting stuck attempting to reread the same content

If I turn code mode off, then it should actually stay disabled and prevent sessions from being able to bypass it

unique_issues.title: Agent invents a circular rollout prerequisite and incorrectly blocks pre-rollout testing
unique_issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

During a long-running integration-testing task in Codex desktop on Windows, the user required testing and resolution of outstanding issues before activating a production pilot. The user explicitly withheld permission to change the production pilot settings.

Codex repeatedly treated activation of that same production pilot as a prerequisite for completing the pre-rollout validation, then cited the withheld activation permission as a reason the goal was blocked. It did not reliably separate pre-rollout acceptance testing from post-activation observation, even after repeated user corrections.

Observed impact: stalled validation, an incorrectly blocked goal state, and repeated user effort to correct the dependency ordering. This report concerns the agent's planning and task-state behavior; it does not establish a defect in the application being tested. No premature production activation is alleged.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The following is a redacted sequence from the observed conversation, not a claim of deterministic reproduction in a fresh session:

1. Give Codex a persistent goal to validate an integration using an isolated test store/account before production rollout.
2. Explicitly instruct it to leave the production pilot unchanged pending signoff.
3. Ask it to continue all validation that does not require activating the production pilot.
4. Observe it promote production sender/workflow activation into a prerequisite for completing validation, and mark/report the goal blocked because activation is not approved.
5. Correct it explicitly: testing must be completed BEFORE the live rollout.
6. Observe the same circular prerequisite recur instead of a corrected dependency plan and continuation of independent test work.

### What is the expected behavior?

Keep pre-rollout acceptance checks, rollout approval/activation, and post-rollout observation distinct and correctly ordered.

Validate whether each claimed blocker actually prevents the next authorized test. Continue independent tests and identify the specific evidence gap for any check that truly requires another environment. Do not turn an explicitly held production action into a prerequisite for all testing or use an invented dependency to set the goal to blocked.

When the user corrects the ordering, update the plan and goal-state reasoning rather than reusing the rejected prerequisite.

### Additional information

Observed October 21, 2026 in Codex desktop on Windows. Exact app/model version was not captured for this report. Root cause is unconfirmed: the transcript demonstrates a reasoning/planning failure, but cannot distinguish model behavior, context handling, or application goal-state orchestration.

Related but distinct: #45370 describes conflicting repository instructions. Here the user's instructions were consistent; the agent introduced the circular dependency.

This report was prepared at the user's explicit request. Business identifiers, store/customer details, credentials, private source, and the full conversation/logs are omitted.

unique_issues.title: Windows desktop app: MCP "Authenticate" button never saves OAuth tokens for a pre-registered Entra ID client; `codex mcp login` works
unique_issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1016.51333

### What subscription do you have?

API key (Azure OpenAI via Microsoft Foundry, custom model provider); no ChatGPT plan

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

For a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server protected by Microsoft Entra ID (using a pre-registered public client, since Entra has no DCR/CIMD), clicking "Authenticate" in Plugins → MCPs completes the browser sign-in ("Authentication complete. You may close this window.") but the tokens are never saved. The server stays signed out: it only receives unauthenticated requests (HTTP 401, no Authorization header), and the Authenticate button keeps showing.

The desktop log records `method=mcpServer/oauth/login` and then no completion, success or error event. On every MCP startup afterwards it logs:

credential storage file fallback completed  credential_kind=mcp store_mode=auto selected_store=secrets actual_store=file operation=load secure_outcome=not_found fallback_reason=secure_entry_missing

followed by: The <server> MCP server is not logged in. Run `codex mcp login <server>`.

Restarting the app does not help. Same result with mcp_oauth_credentials_store = "file" (no .credentials.json is created) and with "keyring".

Workaround: `codex mcp login <server>` (standalone CLI 0.138.0, or the CLI bundled with the app, 0.163.0-alpha.11) prints "Successfully logged in", and the running desktop app starts sending the bearer token within seconds without a restart. So the app can read credentials written by the CLI, but its own Authenticate flow never writes them.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure an Entra ID-protected MCP server with a pre-registered public client in ~/.codex/config.toml:

   [mcp_servers.example-mcp]
   url = "https://<mcp-host>/mcp"
   scopes = ["api://<api-app-id>/<scope>", "offline_access"]

   [mcp_servers.example-mcp.oauth]
   client_id = "<public-client-id>"

   The client has redirect URI http://127.0.0.1/callback/<callback-id> (Mobile and desktop platform). The API app registration lists the MCP URL as an identifier URI, so Entra accepts the resource parameter Codex sends (see #28830).
2. Leave mcp_oauth_credentials_store unset (auto).
3. In the desktop app, open Plugins → MCPs, leave the registration dropdown on Automatic, and click Authenticate.
4. Sign in. The browser shows "Authentication complete".
5. Fully quit and reopen the app, then start a new thread that uses the server.

Result: the server is still not logged in. Running `codex mcp login example-mcp` instead works immediately.

### What is the expected behavior?

The OAuth tokens are persisted and the server starts with an Authorization: Bearer header, the same as after `codex mcp login`, and the Authenticate button disappears.

### Additional information

Possibly related: with mcp_oauth_credentials_store = "keyring", the CLI login fails with:

failed to write OAuth tokens to keyring: Attribute 'password encoded as UTF-16' is longer than platform limit of 2560 chars

Entra access + refresh tokens together exceed the 2,560-byte Windows credential blob limit. If the desktop Authenticate flow writes through a direct keyring path instead of the `secrets` store, that error may be raised and swallowed, which would match the missing completion event.

Related: #28201 (Windows MCP OAuth keyring credentials ignored), #15122 (MCP OAuth login does not persist), #28830 (oauth_resource appends a second resource parameter).

Suggested fixes: surface errors from the desktop Authenticate flow; persist desktop-initiated MCP OAuth logins through the same `secrets` store the CLI uses; make the button reflect the actual login state.

unique_issues.title: `codex mcp get --json` omits the configured `required` flag
unique_issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.163.0`

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant. This is a local configuration command.

### Which model were you using?

Not relevant. The command does not start a model turn.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

zsh 5.9. The terminal does not matter here because the command is non-interactive.

### Codex doctor report

Not included because this reproduction uses an isolated `CODEX_HOME` and does not depend on machine state.

### What issue are you seeing?

`codex mcp get docs --json` omits `required` when the server is configured with `required = true`. The command exits successfully and prints the other server settings, so users and scripts cannot determine from this output whether the server is required.

The CLI reference says this command prints the raw config entry: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run this with Codex CLI 0.163.0:

```sh
test_home="$(mktemp -d)" && printf '%s\n' '[mcp_servers.docs]' 'command = "printf"' 'required = true' > "$test_home/config.toml" && CODEX_HOME="$test_home" codex mcp get docs --json
```

The output is:

```json
{
  "name": "docs",
  "enabled": true,
  "disabled_reason": null,
  "transport": {
    "type": "stdio",
    "command": "printf",
    "args": [],
    "env": null,
    "env_vars": [],
    "cwd": null
  },
  "enabled_tools": null,
  "disabled_tools": null,
  "startup_timeout_sec": null,
  "tool_timeout_sec": null
}
```

`required` is absent.

### What is the expected behavior?

The JSON should include the configured value:

```json
"required": true
```

### Additional information

`McpServerConfig` retains this value in `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:244-248`:

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2a77e82f09212c9e1bbf02656afca5d8172c5f9e/codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs#L244-L248

`run_get` manually builds the JSON object in `codex-rs/cli/src/mcp_cmd.rs:999-1012` and does not copy `server.required`:

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2a77e82f09212c9e1bbf02656afca5d8172c5f9e/codex-rs/cli/src/mcp_cmd.rs#L999-L1012

The smallest fix is to add `"required": server.required` to that object and cover it with an integration test that loads `required = true` and checks the JSON output.

unique_issues.title: [Windows] ChatGPT repeatedly fails to open in one Windows user profile after updating in another
unique_issues.body:
## Summary
On a shared Windows PC with two separate Windows user profiles, ChatGPT repeatedly fails to open in one profile following an update while the other profile is in use. Clicking the app produces no visible window or error. The user reports this recurring with updates and requiring repair.

## Observed sequence
1. ChatGPT is installed for two Windows users on the same PC.
2. An update occurs while one Windows profile is in use.
3. The other Windows user attempts to open ChatGPT, but nothing visibly happens.

## Diagnostic evidence recovered from the repair transcript
The reporting assistant reviewed the local Hermes repair chat and recorded command outputs from October 22, 2026. The user explicitly authorized publishing the following sanitized diagnostic evidence. These are historical repair results, not newly executed diagnostics.

- Package: `OpenAI.Codex`, AppID `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App`.
- Installed/target version: `26.1016.8622.0`; deployment logs show an update from `26.1016.6573.0`.
- Package status before repair: `Servicing`.
- Twelve ChatGPT processes were recorded in the other user's Windows session, with none initially in the affected user's session.
- AppXDeploymentServer events 404/401/459 recorded `0x80073D25`.
- Windows explicitly reported: "The package installation failed because a singleton resource was specified and another user with that package installed is logged in. Please make sure that all active users with the package installed are logged out and retry installation."
- The recorded error identified the other Windows user's SID; all personal account identifiers are omitted here.
- Session enumeration confirmed that the other user's session still existed in a disconnected state while the affected user's session was active.

## Repair recorded by Hermes
An initial attempt to log off the other session failed with access denied. An elevated logoff was then requested, but immediate re-registration retries still failed with `0x80073D25` and the other session was still reported present.

After the user later said to retry, the following re-registration succeeded in the affected user's session:

```powershell
$p = Get-AppxPackage OpenAI.Codex
Add-AppxPackage -Register (Join-Path $p.InstallLocation 'AppxManifest.xml') -DisableDevelopmentMode
```

Hermes launched the app through `shell:AppsFolder\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App` and verified:
- `RegistrationSucceeded=True`
- Package status changed from `Servicing` to `Ok`
- A responding ChatGPT window appeared in the affected user's Windows session.

No app-data reset or deletion was recorded. The precise action that finally cleared the blocking session is not established. The recorded last-boot timestamp remained unchanged through the successful attempt, so the transcript does not demonstrate that a reboot fixed it.

## Expected behavior
Updating ChatGPT should not leave another Windows profile with a silently unlaunchable app. If singleton-component servicing requires the other user to sign out, the update flow should detect this, explain it clearly, and preserve a usable state or provide a supported recovery path.

Please investigate cross-user update/registration with disconnected Windows sessions and singleton components.

## Related reports
Possibly related, not established duplicates: #25770, #25575, #41073.

Exact Windows build was not collected. No raw chat history, names, personal account identifiers, or unrelated logs are attached.

| Oct 21, 2026 07:32:10 | 404 | 26.1016.6573.0 | 0x80073CF9, underlying 0x800700E9, apps need to be closed |
| Oct 21, 2026 09:27:50 | 404 | 26.1016.6573.0 | Same failure |

Representative sanitized event:

```text
AppX Deployment operation failed for package OpenAI.Codex_26.1016.6573.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0 with error 0x80073CF9.
error 0x800700E9: Unable to install because the following apps need to be closed OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App.
```

System / Service Control Manager also records:

- Oct 21, 2026 07:32:09, event 7040: ChatGPT service start type changed from automatic to disabled.
- Oct 21, 2026 09:31:19, event 7045: ChatGPT sandbox service installed from package 26.1016.6573.0, automatic, LocalSystem.

The logs do not identify who initiated the startup-type change. No such change was made during this investigation.

## Separate startup evidence

Desktop logs show repeated policy-read timeouts on October 19 through 22. For example, October 22:

```text
2026-10-22T10:53:00.994Z info [StdioConnection] stdio_transport_spawned argsCount=4 coreRuntimeInUse=false executablePath=<LOCALAPPDATA>\OpenAI\Codex\bin\6257d9e8f63c0f2b\codex.exe pid=19108
2026-10-22T10:53:33.113Z warning Desktop startup policy read failed attempt=1 phase=policy-read reason=timeout retrying=true
2026-10-22T10:53:35.112Z info [StdioConnection] stdio_transport_spawned argsCount=4 coreRuntimeInUse=false executablePath=<LOCALAPPDATA>\OpenAI\Codex\bin\6257d9e8f63c0f2b\codex.exe pid=22296
2026-10-22T10:54:03.053Z warning Desktop startup policy read failed attempt=2 phase=policy-read reason=timeout retrying=false
```

These timeouts are confirmed. Their causal connection to the sandbox-service workaround and AppX deployment failures is not established.

A read-only check of the current `state_5.sqlite` reports `backfill_state.status = complete`. The stale running-backfill condition described in #56389 was not present at collection time.

## Expected behavior and requested investigation

- Desktop updates should coordinate shutdown and restart of their packaged sandbox service and release old package resources without requiring Task Manager intervention.
- Startup should recover from a stale or nonresponsive service, or show an actionable recovery message.
- Investigate whether service lifecycle or old-package handles explain this repeated failure and the observed force-close workaround.
- Correlate the startup policy-read timeout sequence separately; do not assume it has the same cause.
- Provide a supported recovery that preserves local chats, credentials, skills, and project files.

Related reports, with no assertion of identical root cause: [#25770](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25770), [#53132](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53132), and startup-timeout report [#56389](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/56389).

Only selected sanitized evidence is included. No raw logs, private repositories, usernames, credentials, account identifiers, or conversation contents are attached.

unique_issues.title: Windows 10: FrameArrived timed out when capturing windows with Computer Use
unique_issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1016.62342

### What subscription do you have?

Plano pago de R$39,90

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10

### What issue are you seeing?

Olá, equipe do Codex!

Estou enfrentando um problema com a captura automática de tela do Computer Use no Windows 10.

**Ambiente**
- Sistema operacional: Windows 10
- Aplicativo: Codex Desktop
- Versão: 26.1016.62342
- Ferramenta de controle: `@oai/sky` versão 0.7.12
- Aplicativos testados: Adobe Lightroom Classic e Bloco de Notas

**Descrição do problema**

O Codex consegue identificar as janelas abertas e interagir com elas, mas falha ao capturar a tela. O erro apresentado é:

`FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel`

O mesmo problema ocorre tanto no Lightroom Classic quanto no Bloco de Notas.

**Testes realizados**
- A captura manual do Windows com `Win + Shift + S` funciona normalmente.
- Reiniciei o aplicativo Codex.
- Reiniciei o driver gráfico usando `Win + Ctrl + Shift + B`.
- Testei a captura em diferentes aplicativos.
- O Codex continua apresentando o mesmo erro.

**Impacto**

Preciso utilizar o Computer Use para automatizar edições de fotografias no Adobe Lightroom Classic. Como a captura automática não funciona, o Codex não consegue visualizar os controles da interface e executar esse fluxo com segurança.

**Solicitação**

Gostaria de saber se existe uma correção conhecida ou uma solução recomendada para esse problema no Windows 10. Posso fornecer logs adicionais, se necessário.

Obrigado!

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open Codex Desktop on Windows 10.
2. Open Adobe Lightroom Classic.
3. Ask Codex to capture or inspect the Lightroom window using Computer Use.
4. Observe the error: `FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel`.
5. Repeat the test with Windows Notepad.
6. The same error occurs in Notepad, even though Windows manual screenshot capture (`Win + Shift + S`) works.
7. Restart Codex and the graphics driver, then repeat the test. The issue persists.

### What is the expected behavior?

Computer Use should successfully capture and display screenshots of open application windows on Windows 10, including Adobe Lightroom Classic and Notepad.

It should allow Codex to inspect the interface and interact with the applications without timing out.

Since manual screenshot capture works correctly in Windows, the automated capture mechanism should also work without repeatedly returning `FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel`.

### Additional information

Environment:
- OS: Windows 10
- Codex Desktop version: 26.1016.62342
- Computer Use runtime: @oai/sky 0.7.12
- Applications tested: Adobe Lightroom Classic and Windows Notepad

The issue occurs in multiple applications, not only Lightroom.

Manual screenshot capture using Windows + Shift + S works correctly. However, Computer Use repeatedly fails with `FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel`.

Restarting Codex and resetting the graphics driver with Windows + Ctrl + Shift + B did not resolve the issue.

No system files or application executables have been modified. I have not applied any unofficial patches.

unique_issues.title: Windows: timeout when sending messages between Codex windows
unique_issues.body:
Rapporten innehåller inga användarprompter, chattnamn, chatt-ID:n, klient-ID:n eller användarspecifika sökvägar.

## Miljö

- Windows, installerad produktionsutgåva.
- Appens uppdateringskontroll: installerad version 26.1021.31345, build 21828, release channel prod, status up_to_date den 24 oktober 2026.
- Windows-paket: OpenAI.Codex_26.1021.3705.0_x64.
- Två öppna huvudfönster med flera aktiva lokala chattar.

## Användarsymtom

Att skicka text från ett fönster som följer en chatt ger ibland toasten Error submitting message / timeout. Felet inträffar också utan bildbilaga. Samma chatt accepterade senare ett meddelande från ägarfönstret; turn/start fick svar utan fel på 282 ms och meddelandet samt assistentens svar verifierades i historiken.

Fem skickfel från samma följarfönster registrerades inom cirka sju minuter. Ytterligare ett fel inträffade senare. Andra lokala chattar kunde samtidigt använda thread/resume och turn/start.

## Oberoende, läsande reproduktion

En tillfällig IPC-klient använde endast initialize, thread-owner-discovery och thread-follower-read-model-settings. Den annonserade canHandle=false för samtliga inkommande upptäcktsförfrågningar. Den skickade inga chattmeddelanden, gjorde inga inställningsändringar och tog inte över ägarskap.

Försök 1, 24 oktober 2026 07:16 UTC:

| Förfrågan | Chatt A | Kontrollchatt B |
|---|---:|---:|
| thread-owner-discovery | success, 37 ms | success, 18 ms |
| riktad thread-follower-read-model-settings till hittad ägare | no-client-found, 5194 ms | success, 419 ms |

Försök 2, 07:19 UTC, utan ändrad produktkod eller konfiguration: samma ägare för chatt A; upptäckt 13 ms och läsning 11 ms. Tre ytterligare prov 07:20 UTC lyckades; läsningen för A tog 4, 12 respektive 2 ms. Felet är intermittent. Senare framgång är inte bevis för reparation.

## Avgränsning från installerad kod

- IpcClient.sendRequest har standardbudget 5000 ms och kan kasta Error("timeout").
- Router.findClientForRequest gör en separat klientupptäckt även när targetClientId redan är känt.
- Ägarupptäckt kan svara från ett cachelagrat ownedThreads-set, medan efterföljande canHandle för följaroperationer använder getThreadRole via fönstrets view service med en separat budget.
- Resultaten är förenliga med en fördröjd eller misslyckad kontroll vid den senare gränsen. De bevisar inte varför kontrollen blir fördröjd; lång huvudtrådspaus, RPC-transport och annan timing måste skiljas med instrumentering hos produktägaren.
- Den installerade koden har alternativet runAppServerManagerInMain, men startkoden kräver !app.isPackaged och CODEX_APP_SERVER_MANAGER_IN_MAIN=1. Det är inte en fungerande användarinställning för den installerade produktionsutgåvan.

## Föreslagen fortsatt felsökning hos produktägaren

Instrumentera varje steg med samma request-ID: avsändarkö, riktad klientupptäckt, canHandle/getThreadRole över view-service-gränsen, faktisk vidarebefordran och mottagarens svar. Skilj discovery-timeout från en operation som redan skickats. Lägg till ett regressionstest där ägarupptäckt lyckas men nästa rollkontroll fördröjs.

En permanent rättning behöver robust ägarskap och kommunikation även när ett ägarfönster är belastat eller inaktivt. Återförsök av meddelandesändning måste skyddas mot dubbla meddelanden och okänt leveransutfall. Testa också ägarbyte under pågående tur utan avbrott och utan att tappa eller duplicera meddelanden.

## Godkännandekriterier

- Fönster B kan skicka till en chatt som ägs i A, och motsatt riktning fungerar.
- Båda fönstren kan fortsätta andra sessioner under testet.
- Bakgrundsläge, fokusskifte och ägarbyte förlorar inte förfrågningar.
- Varje accepterat användarmeddelande finns exakt en gång i historiken.
- Ingen omstart, processavslutning eller skyddsförsämring krävs som normal återhämtning.

## Närliggande rapporter, inte bevis för samma orsak

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/56673 beskriver låsta schedulerplatser och köavvisningar i Windows. Den aktuella appsessionens logg innehöll inga app_server_client_request_queue_rejected vid kontrollen; den rapportens specifika felbild är därför inte verifierad här.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25914 efterfrågar en stödd koppling till redan aktiva Desktop-sessioner. Det är ett närliggande integrationsproblem, inte samma reproduktion som här.
- Officiell rapporteringsväg: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting#feedback-and-logs

unique_issues.title: [Windows Remote SSH] Native Windows-to-Windows OpenSSH requires global Git Bash shell override and manual socket ACL repair (CLI 0.164.0)
unique_issues.body:
## Summary

I reproduced two independent native-Windows Remote SSH bootstrap problems in **Codex Desktop connecting from one Windows PC to another Windows PC**. I ultimately achieved a working Codex Desktop SSH connection, but only after (1) globally replacing the Windows OpenSSH server's default shell with Git Bash and (2) repairing the native Windows app-server control-socket directory's ACL.

**Request:** Make native Windows OpenSSH hosts first-class SSH remotes with a Windows-aware bootstrap and safe app-server socket initialization. A user should not need Git Bash, WSL, or a machine-wide OpenSSH shell override.

This report documents a **verified end-to-end working result with remote `codex-cli 0.164.0`** and the exact transition from failures to success. It is related to, rather than intended to supersede, #26164, #22965, #31390 and #44581.

## Environment

- **Client:** Codex Desktop on Windows, using `Settings → Connections → SSH`.
- **Remote host:** native Windows 11, build `10.0.26300.9711`, Windows optional-feature OpenSSH Server, no WSL.
- **Network:** private LAN (host address redacted).
- **SSH authentication:** Ed25519 public key, working with native Windows OpenSSH. Account is a member of the local Administrators group; Windows uses `%ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys`.
- **Codex CLI on remote:** `0.148.0`, then updated to `0.164.0`.
- **Codex authentication:** `Logged in using ChatGPT`.
- **Windows login shell before workaround:** native cmd/PowerShell.
- **Workaround shell:** Git for Windows Bash, `MINGW64_NT-10.0-26300`.
- All private IPs, keys, user identifiers and credentials omitted.

## Reproduction and observations

### 1. SSH authentication succeeds but Codex bootstrap assumes POSIX

Native OpenSSH is installed, `sshd` is running, key-based SSH works, and the CLI can be invoked remotely. Yet Codex Desktop's initial remote probe sends POSIX shell constructs to the native Windows login shell. This fails with:

```text
'sh' is not recognized as an internal or external command
'[' is not recognized as an internal or external command
```

This happens **after successful SSH public-key authentication**, not because of a network/firewall/key problem.

### 2. Global Git Bash override passes shell probes, but the app-server connection fails

As a workaround, I set these Windows OpenSSH registry values on the remote machine:

```text
HKLM\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH\DefaultShell = C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe
HKLM\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH\DefaultShellCommandOption = -c
HKLM\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH\DefaultShellEscapeArguments = 0
SHELL (machine environment) = /usr/bin/bash
```

After restarting `sshd`, all manual SSH checks succeeded:

```text
ssh <remote> "echo SHELL_OK"
SHELL_OK

ssh <remote> "command -v codex; codex --version; codex login status"
/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/npm/codex
codex-cli 0.148.0
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

However, Codex Desktop continued to show **`socket hang up`**.

### 3. CLI 0.164.0 gives a precise ACL failure

After updating the native Windows CLI to `0.164.0`, I ran the app-server diagnostic as the **non-elevated** Windows user. Before fixing the ACL:

```text
codex app-server daemon start
Error: app server did not become ready on C:\Users\<user>\.codex\app-server-control\app-server-control.sock

Managed app-server stderr:
Error: socket directory is not private to the current user

codex app-server daemon version
No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it. (os error 10061)
```

The control directory's original ACL was:

```text
Owner: <remote>\<user>
AreAccessRulesProtected: False
Access rule count: 104
```

The large inherited DACL included additional principals, so the security validation correctly rejected it.

One more diagnostic: starting `codex app-server daemon` from an *elevated* terminal was also intentionally rejected:

```text
Error: start the Windows daemon from a non-elevated terminal;
shared clients must not inherit administrator privileges
```

This makes a non-elevated native-Windows app-server lifecycle important.

### 4. Repairing ONLY the control directory ACL makes the native app-server start

I backed up the original control-directory security descriptor and replaced the directory ACL with a protected, inheritable **current-user-only FullControl** rule (without changing Codex credentials or weakening system-wide security). Verified afterward:

```text
Owner: <remote>\<user>
AreAccessRulesProtected: True
Access rule count: 1
Rule: <current user>, FullControl, not inherited
```

Now, from a non-elevated shell:

```text
codex app-server daemon start
{"status":"started","managedCodexVersion":"0.164.0", ...}

codex app-server daemon version
{"status":"running","appServerVersion":"0.164.0", ...}
```

After the SSH key and socket configuration were corrected, **Codex Desktop successfully connected to the native Windows remote**. This is a confirmed working Windows-to-Windows Remote SSH configuration, although it still relies on the Git Bash default-shell override and manual ACL repair.

## Expected behavior / acceptance criteria

1. **Native Windows bootstrap:** If the SSH target is Windows using its default `cmd.exe` or PowerShell shell, Codex Desktop must not unconditionally execute `sh`, POSIX `[`, `umask`, `mkdir -p`, etc. Provide a Windows-aware probe/bootstrap path while continuing to use **OpenSSH as the secure transport**.
2. **No machine-wide shell override:** Git Bash, WSL, changing `HKLM\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH\DefaultShell`, and setting `SHELL=/usr/bin/bash` should **not** be prerequisites.
3. **Secure socket ownership:** The component that owns the Windows app-server control directory should create it with the protected current-user-only DACL expected by the native CLI. Do not weaken or bypass the Windows security validation. In particular, Desktop must not pre-create the directory using POSIX semantics that produce an inherited DACL (see #44581).
4. **Non-elevated lifecycle:** The application should launch or reuse the remote native Windows app-server under a non-elevated user, without requiring elevation as a workaround.
5. **Tests:** Cover Windows OpenSSH `cmd.exe`/PowerShell and POSIX/Linux targets; first-run socket creation and existing-directory cases; explicit rejection of broad ACLs; remote CLI discovery; app-server proxy and WebSocket initialization; and Windows-native project paths.
6. **Actionable errors:** Distinguish incompatible login shell, unsafe socket-directory ACL, and actual SSH authentication failures rather than showing only `SSH connection failed` / `socket hang up`.

## Notes

- Windows OpenSSH is **already the SSH transport** in this setup. The missing capability is **native Windows shell/bootstrap and app-server/socket handling**, not an alternative SSH server.
- This is a firsthand reproduction and successful workaround report; I have **not** demonstrated that simply fixing the ACL also removes the separate shell-compatibility problem.
- Relevant preceding discussions: #26164 (POSIX bootstrap), #31390 (native Windows Remote SSH support), #22965 (Git Bash + proxy failure), #44581 (Desktop-created insecure Windows socket directory), #52190 (non-elevated daemon behavior).
- Can provide additional sanitized logs and ACL diagnostics if maintainers need a focused regression test case.

unique_issues.title: TUI `/clear` leaves the previous thread's stdio MCP servers running (one extra MCP set per `/clear`)
unique_issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.164.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT $100/month plan

### Which model were you using?

GPT-6.1-Sol (medium)

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Orca terminal (Codex launched as `codex --no-daemon ...` in an Orca pane)

### Codex doctor report

Not attached.

### What issue are you seeing?

Every `/clear` in the TUI starts a new set of configured stdio MCP servers, but the MCP servers owned by the previous thread are never terminated. They stay alive as children of the same Codex process until Codex exits.

Two stdio MCP servers are configured globally:

```toml
[mcp_servers.context7]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]

[mcp_servers.node_repl]
command = "/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/cua_node/bin/node_repl"
```

Process counts on the Codex terminal after each `/clear` + one prompt (`node_repl` spawns one child, so one set = 2 `node_repl` + 1 `context7-mcp`):

| point | `context7-mcp` | `node_repl` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| start | 1 | 2 |
| after 1st `/clear` | 2 | 4 |
| after 2nd `/clear` | 3 | 6 |
| after 3rd `/clear` | 4 | 8 |

The leftover processes are not orphaned. Their parent is still the live Codex process, so they are only cleaned up when that Codex process exits. In a long-lived session that is reused with `/clear` (we reuse reviewer sessions this way), one session accumulated 8 sets before we killed them by hand.

#19753 made thread shutdown terminate stdio MCP servers, but `/clear` appears to open a new thread without shutting down the old one, similar to the `thread/unsubscribe` retention described in #39783.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure one or more stdio MCP servers in `~/.codex/config.toml` (any server works, e.g. `context7` above).
2. Start `codex` in a terminal and note its TTY (`ps -o tty= -p <codex pid>`).
3. Count MCP processes on that TTY: `ps -t <tty> -o command= | grep -c '[c]ontext7-mcp$'`.
4. Run `/clear`, then send any prompt (e.g. `Reply with the single word OK.`) and wait for the reply.
5. Count again. Repeat steps 4 and 5.

The count grows by one MCP set per `/clear`.

### What is the expected behavior?

`/clear` shuts down the previous thread's MCP servers (or reuses them for the new thread), so the number of MCP processes stays constant across `/clear`.

### Additional information

Related: #21984 (MCP servers start eagerly per session), #39783 (retained ephemeral threads keep MCP stacks alive), #19753 (thread shutdown terminates stdio MCP servers).

unique_issues.title: [BUG] Send Message to Proceed While Running Hangs Roo
unique_issues.body:
### Problem (one or two sentences)

When Roo launches an app (directly or via a script) we are shown the `Proceed While Running` and `Kill Command` button while Roo waits for the process to complete. We are allowed to enter a message and click send, but at that point Roo hangs will all inputs disabled.

### Context (who is affected and when)

Everyone who wants to collab with Roo on a running background launched via the terminal.

### Reproduction steps

Create an app or script that does something interesting (e.g. starts a web app) and have Roo launch it. Do not click on the `Proceed While Running` button, but rather type a message (e.g. Let's launch a browser and take a look at that together!)  and click the send button. All inputs are disabled and Roo hangs.

Workaround/Recovery from this state:
To recover you have to click the `New Task` button to close the session, then come back into the session. You'll find now a `Resume Task` button and the message controls are enabled. Type the message again because it's not in the history. Click Send.

### Expected result

Roo proceeds while the task is running and receives the message and the message is stored in the message history.

### Actual result

The Roo harness hangs requiring the workaround described above

Bad request: Index required but not found for "pathSegments.5" of one of the following types: [keyword].

unique_issues.title: [BUG][A11Y] Roo-Code steals focus on load when using VSCode over SSH (WCAG 3.2.1, 3.2.2 violation)
unique_issues.body:
## Description

When running VSCode over SSH, Roo-Code can take 1-2 seconds to fully load. During this delay, users may start typing in other parts of VSCode (e.g., the integrated terminal). When Roo-Code finishes loading, it automatically steals focus to its input text box, causing the user to inadvertently type into Roo-Code instead of their intended target.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect to a remote server via SSH in VSCode
2. Open VSCode (or reload the window)
3. Immediately start typing in the integrated terminal while Roo-Code is still loading
4. Observe that when Roo-Code loads, focus shifts to the Roo-Code input box
5. Notice that your terminal input is now being typed into the Roo-Code text box instead

## Expected Behavior

Roo-Code should not automatically steal focus from other elements when it finishes loading. Focus should remain where the user placed it.

## Actual Behavior

Roo-Code takes focus when it loads, interrupting the user's workflow and causing them to type in the wrong location.

## Accessibility Impact

This behavior violates WCAG 2.1 accessibility criteria:

- **WCAG 3.2.1 (On Focus)**: Components should not initiate a change of context when they receive focus
- **WCAG 3.2.2 (On Input)**: Changing the setting of a user interface component should not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised

These are Level A criteria, meaning they are fundamental accessibility requirements.

## Environment

- VSCode: Remote SSH connection
- Roo-Code: Latest version
- Network: Variable latency (SSH over network)

## Suggested Fix

- Do not auto-focus the Roo-Code input box on extension load
- If auto-focus is desired, add a user setting to disable this behavior
- Consider checking if the user is already interacting with another element before taking focus

## Related Issues

This is distinct from previous focus-stealing issues (#8840, #2122, #4784) which were about focus stealing during file edits. This issue is specifically about initial extension load.

---

**Labels**: bug, accessibility, a11y, WCAG
**Priority**: Medium (affects user experience and accessibility compliance)

unique_issues.title: [ENHANCEMENT] Ability to select specific terminal instance when using @terminal to prevent context pollution
unique_issues.body:
### Problem (one or two sentences)

Currently, using @terminal attaches the output from all active terminal instances indiscriminately. This floods the LLM context with irrelevant logs (e.g., from background processes or installation tabs), wasting tokens and degrading model performance.

### Context (who is affected and when)

This affects users working with multiple terminal tabs (e.g., one for server logs, another for git commands, and a third for package installation). When a user needs the LLM to analyze an error in just one specific tab, they are currently forced to close all other tabs to isolate the context, which disrupts the workflow.

### Desired behavior (conceptual, not technical)

When invoking @terminal, the interface should allow the user to select a specific open terminal instance by its name. The context sent to the LLM should be strictly limited to the logs/output of that selected instance, rather than merging all open terminals.

### Constraints / preferences (optional)

It would be ideal to keep the UI selection quick, perhaps appearing as a sub-list when typing @terminal, or allowing a syntax like @terminal:name.

### Request checklist

- [x] I've searched existing Issues and Discussions for duplicates
- [x] This describes a specific problem with clear context and impact

### Roo Code Task Links (optional)

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria (optional)

1.User can distinguish between multiple open terminal instances in the context picker.

2.Selecting a specific terminal sends only that instance's buffer to the LLM.

3.Token usage is reduced by excluding irrelevant terminal outputs.

### Proposed approach (optional)

Modify the @terminal context provider to enumerate active VS Code terminal instances. Instead of a single action that grabs all buffers, present a list of instances (using window.terminals API) for the user to pick from.

### Trade-offs / risks (optional)

This adds a slight UI layer to the selection process. To mitigate friction for users who do want everything, an "All Terminals" option could be retained as a choice.

unique_issues.title: Add ability to restore workspace to initial task state
unique_issues.body:
## Problem

Users cannot easily restore their workspace to the initial state when a task was created. When an agent makes changes during a task—or multiple tasks build on each other—there is no quick way to reset the workspace to the state it was in at the start of a specific task.

## Impact

Users who want a "clean slate" from when a task began must manually revert files or use git commands outside Roo Code. This is especially frustrating when:
- An agent goes down an unproductive path and makes many file changes
- Users want to try a different approach from the same starting point
- Changes from subsequent tasks need to be undone to retry the original task

unique_issues.title: [ENHANCEMENT] Rename attempt_completion tool to notify_about_the_completion (prevents premature “done” behavior + improves UX semantics)
unique_issues.body:
### Problem (one or two sentences)

Users and LLM agents are misled by the terminal tool name attempt_completion, which implies an external or fallible completion step. This causes premature “done” messages even when required subtasks or validations are not finished.

### Context (who is affected and when)

This affects anyone using Roo Code in agentic workflows, especially multi-step tasks with tool calls and validations. It is most visible when the agent is instructed to wait for specific conditions or confirmations before finishing, yet still emits a completion message early.

### Desired behavior (conceptual, not technical)

When an agent finishes, it should clearly report that the task is complete — not “attempt” completion. The terminal tool should communicate finality and ownership by the agent, reducing premature termination and user confusion.

### Constraints / preferences (optional)

No behavior change required; naming and description clarity is sufficient
Keep semantics obvious to both humans and LLMs
Avoid language that implies retries, delegation, or uncertainty

### Request checklist

- [x] I've searched existing Issues and Discussions for duplicates
- [x] This describes a specific problem with clear context and impact

### Roo Code Task Links (optional)

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed approach (optional)

Rename the tool to something that reflects its real role as a terminal notification.

Recommended name:

* **`notify_about_the_completion`**

Other acceptable alternatives:

* `notify_completion`
* `notify_task_completion`
* `report_completion`
* `publish_result`

At minimum, removing the word **`attempt`** would already eliminate most of the confusion.

#### Suggested description (example)

> Use this tool to notify the user that the task has been completed and to deliver the final result.
> This tool represents a terminal action: once called, the agent considers the task finished and will not perform further tool calls unless explicitly re-invoked by the user.

### Trade-offs / risks (optional)

Automatic closure of old issues related to attempt_completion would be trickier to be auto-fixable.

unique_issues.title: [ENHANCEMENT] Adopt agent-trace standard for event emission and observability
unique_issues.body:
### Problem (one or two sentences)

Developers and integrators currently lack a standardized way to observe, log, and visualize Roo Code's internal decision-making process and lifecycle events in real-time using external tools.

### Context (who is affected and when)

This affects contributors and ecosystem developers who want to build advanced debugging tools, visualization dashboards, or analytics layers on top of Roo Code. Currently, understanding exactly what the agent is "thinking" or doing programmatically requires parsing custom logs, which is brittle and limits interoperability with other AI tooling (like what is seen in the Cursor ecosystem).

### Desired behavior (conceptual, not technical)

Roo Code should optionally emit events (such as "planning started," "tool executed," or "file modified") using the standardized agent-trace format. This would allow any tool capable of reading this standard to automatically generate visual traces and logs of Roo's work without needing custom integration logic.

### Constraints / preferences (optional)

Performance: Tracing should have negligible impact on the agent's speed.

Opt-in: This should likely be configurable (e.g., a setting to "Enable Advanced Tracing") to avoid log noise for standard users.

Compatibility: The implementation should align with the schema defined in https://github.com/cursor/agent-trace.

### Request checklist

- [x] I've searched existing Issues and Discussions for duplicates
- [x] This describes a specific problem with clear context and impact

### Roo Code Task Links (optional)

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria (optional)

Given the user has enabled "Agent Tracing" in settings
When Roo Code executes a task loop (e.g., analyses a file, generates a thought, uses a tool)
Then it should emit a JSON event matching the `agent-trace` schema
And these events should include timestamps, event types (Run, Span, Generation), and relevant payloads
But it should not expose sensitive API keys in the trace payload

### Proposed approach (optional)

Review the specification at https://github.com/cursor/agent-trace.

Integrate the agent-trace library (or replicate the schema if a lightweight implementation is preferred).

Instrument the main agent loop in Roo Code to emit spans:

Root Span: The main task prompt.

Child Spans: Individual steps in the loop (planning, tool execution, response generation).

Map Roo's internal log structures to the agent-trace event types.

### Trade-offs / risks (optional)

Overhead: Adding detailed instrumentation adds a slight maintenance burden to keep the trace logic in sync with the agent's core loop logic.

Payload Size: Traces can get large for long-running tasks; we may need a mechanism to rotate logs or limit trace depth.

unique_issues.title: [BUG] Checkpoints nested-repo detection misses submodule/worktree .git files and can false-positive via symlink follow
unique_issues.body:
## Summary

`ShadowCheckpointService.getNestedGitRepository()` has three correctness issues that cause it to miss nested git repositories (false negatives) or incorrectly detect repositories outside the workspace (false positives).

## Impact

- **False negatives:** Git submodules and worktrees use a `.git` *file* (not directory) containing a `gitdir:` pointer. The current search pattern (`**/.git/HEAD`) only finds `.git` directories. Submodule/worktree-style nested repos are completely missed, allowing checkpoints to initialize when they should be disabled.
- **False positives:** The `--follow` flag causes ripgrep to traverse symlinks outside the workspace boundary, potentially detecting git repositories that are not actually nested in the workspace.
- **Brittle path matching:** The current filter uses `includes(".git/HEAD")` and `startsWith(".git/")` for path classification, which is imprecise across platforms and path formats.

## Reproduction

**False negative (submodule case):**
1. Create a workspace with a git submodule (the submodule directory will contain a `.git` file with `gitdir: ...` content instead of a `.git` directory)
2. Initialize checkpoints
3. Observe that the nested repo is not detected and checkpoints proceed

**False positive (symlink case):**
1. Create a workspace containing a symlink that points to a directory outside the workspace
2. The external directory (or its ancestors) contains a `.git` repository
3. Initialize checkpoints
4. Observe that `--follow` causes ripgrep to traverse the symlink and detect the external repo as "nested"

## Expected behavior

- Nested repos inside the workspace are detected consistently, regardless of whether they use a `.git` directory or a `.git` pointer file
- Paths outside the workspace are not considered
- Root-level `.git` (directory or file) is excluded from detection

## Actual behavior

- `.git` pointer files (submodules/worktrees) are missed entirely

unique_issues.title: [BUG] Queued user messages auto-approve tool execution without explicit confirmation
unique_issues.body:
### Problem

A user message arriving before or during a tool approval prompt is treated as `yesButtonClicked`, causing tool execution without an explicit approval click.

### Reproduction

1. Start a task that will trigger a tool approval prompt (e.g., file write with auto-approve disabled)
2. Send any message while the approval prompt is active (or have one queued before the prompt appears)
3. Observe: tool execution proceeds as if the user clicked "Yes"

### Expected behavior

Approval requires an explicit Yes/No button click. Queued user messages should remain in the queue and be processed after the approval interaction resolves.

### Actual behavior

Queued messages are dequeued and interpreted as `yesButtonClicked` for approval-type asks (`tool`, `command`, `browser_action_launch`, `use_mcp_server`).

### Root cause

`Task.ts` `ask()` contains two sites where queued messages bypass approval:

1. **Immediate path** (~line 1591): When `ask()` is called and a message is already queued, it dequeues and calls `handleWebviewAskResponse("yesButtonClicked", ...)` for approval-type asks
2. **Polling loop** (~line 1620): While waiting for user response in `pWaitFor`, if a message arrives during any 100ms polling interval, it auto-approves with `yesButtonClicked`

### Related issues

- #11211 — original report of this behavior
- #11210 — parallel tool calls compound this risk (rapid sequential approval prompts + queued message auto-approval)
- #11095 — broader auto-approve safety concerns

unique_issues.title: Tool execution fails: attempt_completion missing nativeArgs for Z-AI and Ollama after provider migrations
unique_issues.body:
## Description

**Regression window:** Nightly build 0.0.7995 (Feb 8) works; 0.0.8003 (Feb 9) fails.

**Symptom:** Tool execution fails with `Invalid tool call for 'attempt_completion': missing nativeArgs` for Z-AI GLM variants (GLM-4.7, GLM-4.5-air, GLM-4.7-flash) and Ollama Qwen variants (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-Uncensored:Q4_0). OpenRouter route (e.g., Pony Alpha / GLM via OpenRouter) works correctly.

## Root cause

Two issues identified:

### 1. Strict OpenAI tool schema mutation applied to non-OpenAI models

The Z-AI handler (`zai.ts`) and Ollama handler (`native-ollama.ts`) wrap tool schemas with `convertToolsForOpenAI()` before passing to `convertToolsForAiSdk()`. This adds `strict: true`, forces all properties to `required`, and sets `additionalProperties: false` -- constraints that GLM and Qwen models do not reliably support. The result is malformed or missing tool call arguments.

The OpenRouter handler does **not** apply this wrapper, passing tools directly to `convertToolsForAiSdk()`. This explains why the same model family works via OpenRouter but fails via Z-AI or Ollama.

### 2. Truthy check on attempt_completion.result rejects empty strings

`NativeToolCallParser.ts` uses `if (args.result)` instead of `if (args.result !== undefined)` to gate `attempt_completion` nativeArgs construction. An empty string `""` is falsy, so `result: ""` produces missing nativeArgs even when the tool call arguments are otherwise valid. This affects both the streaming and finalize parse paths.

## Proposed fix

- **PR 1 (hardening):** Change truthy check to existence check (`!== undefined`) in both parser paths, with regression tests.
- **PR 2 (behavior fix):** Remove `convertToolsForOpenAI()` wrapper from Z-AI and Ollama handlers, aligning them with the working OpenRouter path.

## Reproduction

1. Configure Z-AI provider with GLM-4.7 (or Ollama with Qwen2.5-Coder)
2. Start any task that triggers tool use (e.g., ask to read a file)
3. Observe error: `Invalid tool call for 'attempt_completion': missing nativeArgs`
4. Switch to OpenRouter with the same model family -- works correctly

unique_issues.title: OpenRouter proxy: tool calls silently dropped after AI SDK migration (tool-call event ignored)
unique_issues.body:
## Description

When using OpenRouter as a proxy, tool calls are silently dropped after the OpenRouter AI SDK migration (PR #10778, Feb 9), producing false "Model Response Incomplete / failed to use any tools" errors. This affects all models routed through OpenRouter and causes retry loops with significant cost inflation.

## Root cause

Two interacting issues:

1. **`processAiSdkStreamPart()` ignores `tool-call` events** (ai-sdk.ts line 491). The handler was designed to rely solely on `tool-input-start/delta/end` lifecycle events for tool delivery.

2. **`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider` v2.1.1 has incomplete lifecycle emission:**
   - Incrementally streamed tool calls: emits `tool-input-start` + `tool-input-delta` but never `tool-input-end`
   - Flush-path tool calls: emits only `tool-call` with zero `tool-input-*` events

The combination means tool calls are silently lost. Prior to the AI SDK migration, OpenRouter used the `openai` npm package with `NativeToolCallParser`, which handled tool calls correctly via `delta.tool_calls`.

## Timeline

| Date | Version | Event |
|------|---------|-------|
| Jan 15 | v3.41.0 | OpenRouter uses `openai` SDK + `NativeToolCallParser`. Works fine. |
| Jan 20 | — | XML tool calling removed (`8de9337e6`, PR #10841) |
| Jan 23 | v3.42.0 | First release without XML tools. OpenRouter still uses `openai` SDK. Still works. |
| Jan 28 | — | `src/api/transform/ai-sdk.ts` first created (`fe722dad2`, PR #11047) |
| Feb 6 | v3.47.3 | Latest numbered release. OpenRouter still uses `openai` SDK. |
| **Feb 9** | **unreleased** | **OpenRouter migrated to AI SDK** (PR #10778). Bug introduced. |
| Feb 11 | unreleased | PR #11420 fix lands |

The true regression boundary is the OpenRouter AI SDK migration (PR #10778, Feb 9), not v3.41.0 → v3.44.0 as originally stated.

## Reproduction

1. Configure any model through OpenRouter (e.g., Sonnet 4.5, Grok)
2. Send a task that requires tool use
3. Observe "failed to use any tools" errors and retry loops
4. Same model via direct provider works correctly

## Environment

- Roo Code: post-AI SDK migration (unreleased, after PR #10778)
- OpenRouter as API proxy
- Any model (not model-specific)

## Expected behavior

Tool calls routed through OpenRouter should be delivered and executed identically to direct provider connections.

unique_issues.title: Todo list lost from system prompt after context condensation
unique_issues.body:
## Bug Description

The todo list is currently only visible to the model via ephemeral `environment_details` content in user messages. After context condensation removes earlier messages, the model loses awareness of outstanding todo items. This can lead to premature task completion — the model believes all work is done because it can no longer see the todo list.

## Expected Behavior

The todo list should be included in the system prompt so it survives context condensation and remains visible to the model throughout the entire task lifecycle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a task with todo items
2. Generate enough conversation to trigger context condensation
3. Observe that the model loses awareness of incomplete todo items

## Impact

Orchestrator mode is particularly affected — when the model loses visibility into incomplete todos after condensation, it may attempt completion while work remains outstanding.

unique_issues.title: Orchestrator can complete tasks prematurely without verifying todo completion
unique_issues.body:
## Bug Description

In orchestrator mode, the model can call `attempt_completion` even when:
1. No todo list exists (no plan was created)
2. Todo items remain incomplete (pending or in_progress)

The existing `preventCompletionWithOpenTodos` setting defaults to `false`, making it opt-in. Orchestrator mode relies on structured delegation through todo lists, so completion without verifying the plan is structurally premature.

After context condensation, the model may lose visibility of outstanding work and attempt completion early. While a separate PR (#11434) addresses the visibility side by including the todo list in the system prompt, completion enforcement is still needed.

## Expected Behavior

In orchestrator mode:
- Completion should be blocked if no todo list exists
- Completion should be blocked if any todo items are not completed
- This should apply regardless of the global `preventCompletionWithOpenTodos` setting

## Impact

Orchestrator mode is designed for multi-step coordination. Premature completion means delegated subtasks may be abandoned or their results never synthesized.
